tieu_de: CHUYFIN OUTSIDE ABOUT VEGAN FEEDING
tom_tat: People often ask about vegetarian food having few varieties, monotonous flavors, and not knowing how to cook without meat. They said that because Buddhists are vegetarian, they buy fake foods like chicken, duck, fish, vegetarian meat, and eat...
noi_dung:
People often ask about vegetarian food having few varieties, monotonous flavors, and not knowing how to cook without meat. They say, because Buddhists are vegetarian but they buy fake foods like chicken, duck, fish, vegetarian meat, eating fake things like that, it's not as good as eating the real thing frankly, which sounds reasonable.
In fact, there are no less than hundreds of types of vegetables, it just depends on the season. Nowadays, there are more and more out-of-season vegetables produced in greenhouses. However, the price is not only expensive but also not a natural product. If I am not a guest coming to eat at home to add a few dishes, I absolutely do not buy greenhouse vegetables. In fact, natural vegetables are the best nutritional foods, combined with beans can completely meet nutritional needs. I often during the main vegetable season, choose some types that can be dried and dried to use in the winter, such as eggplant, string beans, white radish, abalone mushrooms,... Used as a filling, it's quite good, eating with more peace of mind than greenhouse vegetables. Regarding taste, it can be said that a person who truly practices Buddhism and observes the precepts will not be attached to good flavors, because by reciting Buddha's prayers and reading sutras to understand the principles, he will naturally reduce his attachments to money, lust, fame, eating, drinking and sleeping.
One day, you will suddenly discover that the food you cook is very delicious. Not only does your family find it delicious, but guests also compliment it, sometimes it's just cooking cabbage with shredded potatoes. Steaming dumplings and making dumplings, even meat eaters praise the deliciousness, but when they return home
I made it, using the same ingredients, but it didn't taste the same as I did. I often hear people praising the delicious Arhat Chay dish at the temple. Why can't meat-eaters cook such a simple mixed stew to taste like Buddhists cook it? That's because vegetarian Buddha chanters have the support of the God of Food when cooking, helping you add spices. It can be said that it is also the making offerings of the Gods. Not only that, when you go to the market to buy vegetables, the God of Food also silently guides you to buy the vegetables you like. I often buy a bunch of vegetables for one dollar that have probably been left for two days. Maybe God knows I live frugally, so I can often buy them a few times cheaper and still taste just as good. My neighbors also often want to buy this vegetable, but never meet it. Therefore, if you sincerely study Buddha, with the support of demons and gods, when you cultivate to the point of seeing the heavenly eye, you will naturally understand.
"If you endure suffering, your suffering will end; if you enjoy happiness, your happiness will end." I will accept the things that others don't like, without being attached to anything, persistently pursuing them, and I will naturally achieve them.
As for fake meats such as chicken, duck, and fish, they are for those who are just learning Buddhism and are in the process of giving up meat. They are a transitional food, like people who are just starting to quit smoking. When they crave a cigarette, they put a piece of candy in their mouth to soothe their mind. Long-time practitioners who have observed the precepts should not eat this fake animal meat, because when eaten, its appearance already touches the mind, this is also the teaching of Venerable Master Hsuan Hua.
However, if you want to add a few dishes, you can break their shape before cooking. That is also a convenient method. This dish should not be named after an animal, for example, cut fake chicken and duck meat into small square pieces, combine with chestnuts, cashews, peanuts to stir-fry, with
can be called "Bodhi fruit". Imitation seafood such as fish with seaweed, after being chopped, combined with wood ear mushrooms or snow mushrooms, add a little green chili, decorated with two small tomatoes, looks very beautiful, can be called Hai Lien Hoa, if combined with golden enoki mushrooms can be called Golden Sea Lien Hoa, similarly, arbitrary naming is also very interesting.

tieu_de: DO NOT KILL LIVES, SO HOW TO REpell MOSQUITOS AND INSECTS
tom_tat:
Ask: There are mosquitoes, flies, ants, cockroaches, and bedbugs at home. Can you kill them? What should I do if I can't kill it?
Answer: The Buddha in the Brahma Hammock Sutra teaches that: "All living creatures must not be intentionally killed." So...
noi_dung:
Ask: There are mosquitoes, flies, ants, cockroaches, and bedbugs at home. Can you kill them? What should I do if I can't kill it?
Answer: The Buddha in the Brahma Hammock Sutra teaches that: "All living creatures must not be intentionally killed." Therefore, all creatures with life cannot be killed. So what to do? I will tell you two stories:
Câu chuyện thứ nhất: Twelve years ago, I lived in a private house in the city center, where there were a lot of ants. Not only in the kitchen, but also in my office and bedroom, there were ants crawling on me, which was very annoying. Although I used many drugs to kill them, they were ineffective. I even sprinkle a little honey or white sugar in the yard, wait for the ants to gather in one place, then use boiling water from the kettle to kill them. The number of ants killed was countless, but the number of ants in the house not only did not decrease but also increased. To prevent ants from crawling on food in the kitchen, I hang a food basket with a thin wire from the ceiling. Thought the ants wouldn't be able to find it, but the next day when I took the basket down to get the food, it was full of ants! Angry, I put the food basket in the yard, took an old newspaper, burned it and put it in the basket, making a "sky lantern".
After meeting Venerable Dieu Phap, I learned that living things cannot be killed. Even though at that time I still ate "three pure meat" and didn't buy raw chicken or raw fish anymore, I didn't
Never consider ants as "life" because they are so small! Then when I returned home, I faced the ant problem again. When I sprinkled ant killing powder and insecticide on all the windows and doors, I suddenly thought that ants are also life, they certainly also have thoughts, otherwise how can they be so organized and disciplined? I felt very insecure, thinking about my master's teachings, feeling ashamed, suddenly a feeling of fear rose in my heart. The number of ants I have killed over the years is countless, they will sooner or later find me to settle accounts! But now I sprinkled the ant killing powder again, not knowing how many lives it would kill, so I quickly wiped off the poisonous powder, then rinsed it with water.
Because I was alone at home at that time, I kindly talked to the ants crawling back and forth in the yard: "Ant, ant, I didn't know not to kill living creatures before, I killed too many ants. Just now I sprinkled poison again. Even though I washed it off, it may still be left on the windows and doors. Don't crawl there. From now on I will not kill ants anymore, I hope you will not come into my house or kitchen. You can crawl freely in the yard, but if I accidentally kick you to death, don't blame me. It's best for you to stay in the flower garden, there's no danger there. Don't come to my house to bother me, I absolutely won't harm you." Actually, at that time I had never read the scriptures, I just said these words to the ants with kindness, not thinking that if I don't let them into the kitchen, what will they eat?
A few days later, my son said: "Dad, there are no more ants in our house." Actually, I forgot about this a long time ago. When my child said that, I remembered the words I said a few days ago. I started looking for ants in the yard, but didn't see any. I wondered if it was the weather that caused the ants in this area to disappear, so I went to the neighbor's house to see
tried, and surprisingly, their house still had ants! This surprised me greatly, my joy was not because ants had disappeared but because I understood that humans can communicate with other creatures. As long as you say and do things with a sincere heart, there will definitely be an response. If at that time I had known to sprinkle a little food scraps in the flower garden every day, it would have been a source of life for the ants, but I didn't understand, so I just asked them not to go into the kitchen, and they had to move somewhere else.
Since that year, I have lived here for 6 years, and have not seen a single ant appear.
Before taking refuge, I killed creatures, ate meat, drank alcohol, it can be said "every thought, every action is karma, every sin". Why is there this induction? The first is due to sincerity, the second is due to the blessings of Buddha and Bodhisattva. Buddha is great compassion, saving all sentient beings, no matter who they are, with just a little good thought, Buddha will skillfully save that person, leading them from evil to good. The ancients taught: "If you want to bring people into Buddha's wisdom, you must first use desire to guide you." I am the type of person who is ignorant, has no wisdom, and cannot immediately believe through teachings and books. Only the obvious truths can make me believe, and then pursue and practice. This may also be the reason why I later learned how to chant sutras, recite Buddha's name and dedicating merit to sentient beings.
Câu chuyện thứ hai: My junior brother, Guo Pei, came from his hometown of Henan and told the story of how he used the method I taught him to deal with the mouse problem in his house. He also talked to the mouse, apologized and admitted his guilt, promised not to kill mice anymore, then every day in a fixed place, put some leftover food in a plate for the mouse. Initially, mice not only ate the food on the plate but also ate other things and destroyed some furniture. Master Qua Boi said: “Before, I killed rats
too much, you guys hate me right. From now on, I will recite the Great Compassion Mantra 30 times every day, dedicating merit to the rats I have killed, delivering sentient beings onto the path of goodness. About three months later, the mice only ate food in plates on the ground, did not eat other food and did not destroy furniture anymore. One day, Qua Boi's sister came from far away to stay for a while. Seeing him feeding the mice every day, she laughed and did not believe that the mice would listen. She deliberately placed a dumpling on the table after dinner, as a result, the next morning the dumpling was still intact. Repeatedly for three days, the mouse only ate the food in the plate on the ground, which left her speechless. What's even more strange is that after washing her clothes, she put them in the same closet as her brother and sister-in-law's clothes, but the mice only gnawed on her clothes. How do mice differentiate? She had to admit it and promise that when she got home she wouldn't kill mice anymore. After that, my brother's house no longer had mice.
Use a small glass or glass jar and place it over the mosquito. Then use a piece of prepared paper to insert into the mouth of the glass to keep it closed, then move it out the window. Instruct mosquitoes not to bite people, recite Buddha's prayers and let them take refuge in the Three Jewels, then release the mosquitoes out the window. After persistently doing this for a year or two, the number of mosquitoes entering the house is significantly reduced. If you get bitten by a mosquito, it doesn't itch much, just a small spot the size of a millet grain that quickly disappears. For more than ten years, my family has rarely been bitten by mosquitoes, and now I share this method for fellow practitioners to refer to.
The principle is the same as above. Some farmers who practice Buddha Dharma choose to spray water and recite the Great Compassion Mantra 49 times. Others use the three-notice method
day. On the day of spraying, they recite the Great Compassion Mantra many times to pray for the insects. These methods all have certain effectiveness. It is important to have a truly repentant heart. We cannot hope that just reciting a few sutras or mantras will make the insects disappear. "Everything is created by the mind", not created by sutras or mantras. Reciting Buddha, reciting sutras, and reciting mantras are just supporting conditions.
Maybe give three days notice that the house will be cleaned and invite them to move. On the third day, if there are still insects, you can clean them without intentionally killing them. While cleaning, you can chant Buddha, rebirth Mantra, or Great Compassion Mantra to deliverance to small creatures that are accidentally harmed (including when plowing the land). Venerable Dieu Phap said that doing so is the right way and over time there will be no more insects. If you do not eat salty foods and have abandoned desire, when you ask the insects to move away, they will disappear because your merit is great enough to help them escape suffering and enjoy pleasure. Just like a king wants someone to be rich, just a word is enough, while a virtuous person needs to teach the poor how to get rich step by step. Therefore, repentance, observing the precepts, chanting sutras and cultivating virtue are things practitioners must always remember.
“PEOPLE ARE NOT FOR THEMSELVES, YOU ARE TRULY DIFIT”
Ask: “The ancients said: 'If a person does not care for himself, heaven and earth will destroy him', how should this sentence be explained?"
Answer: “May I ask, which ancient person said this? I'm afraid I can't find it in 'Tu Hai' either. Because of my shallow education, the first time I heard this sentence was during the Great Cultural Revolution. In fact, the saying was in the modern opera Hong Dang Ky. When the Japanese invader Khue Son advised Ly Ngoc Hoa to betray the Fatherland, he said this sentence. This is truly the devil used to drag others to hell.
'tru' means to kill or punish, but here it means 'without' or 'without'. When you die, you "don't exist" anymore, that is
„no‟ then. 'Destroy' means completely, finished, empty. Therefore, the correct understanding of the meaning of "people who do not protect themselves will be destroyed by heaven" is: "If man could not for his own good, then heaven would no longer exist and the earth would also be empty." In other words: "If a person does not work for himself, wholeheartedly for the benefit of sentient beings, then heaven and earth will not be able to control him, he will go beyond the Three Realms, not within the Five Elements, and will transcend the realm of sainthood."
Discussion: In Vietnam, young people also share a common saying: "The elders teach - children don't play, old people fall apart." It is true that as layman Qua Khanh explained - demons use to lure others to hell. I don't know which grandparents or parents teach their children and grandchildren like that but ask the elders to teach it.
Young people who do not cultivate morality, train themselves, learn good and reasonable things, but instead learn the habit of playing around and hanging out, are truly a disaster for their families and society. Once damaged, there may be no longer old age.

tieu_de: FUNERAL CEREMONY FOLLOWING THE FOLLOWING OF Buddha
tom_tat: Ask: Currently, in the press there are often reports about "spectacular" funerals, which are both expensive and affect traffic and urban beauty, and are also not suitable for the current era. But the funeral organizers h...
noi_dung:
Ask: Currently, in the press there are often reports about "spectacular" funerals, which are both expensive and affect traffic and urban beauty, and are also not suitable for the current era. But those who organized this grand funeral said this was filial piety. I see that countries that believe in Jesus and countries that believe in Islam are not as big as ours. According to Buddhism, how to organize a funeral properly and with filial piety?
Answer: Our country encourages atheism, advising people to believe that only we are the masters of changing the nation's destiny and our own destiny, which is also consistent with the ethics of Buddhism. Although the vast majority of people do not believe in the theory of "six paths samsara" of Buddhism, many people have the habit of doing things similar to Buddhist principles when their loved ones die. For example, believing that humans have a soul (Buddha religion calls it consciousness), after death they must go through periods of loss (7 days, 14 days, 21 days, up to 49 days). This is also drawn from the Ksitigarbha Sutra of Buddhism. And there are many misconceptions and illegal folk habits such as believing that the dead become ghosts, burning paper money, paper money, paper people, paper horses, paper cows, using chicken, duck, and fish to worship demons.
So how to organize a funeral to benefit the deceased, please see the sutra text in the Ksitigarbha Sutra: "All living beings in the present and future, at the time of death, if
Hearing a name of Buddha, a name of Bodhisattva, a name of Bich Chi Buddha, regardless of guilt or innocence, will be liberated.
If there are men and women who do not cultivate kindness (do good deeds) while living, and commit many sins. After death, their relatives, big and small, create welfare for them and do all the holy things, then out of the seven merits, the dead person will only get one, and the remaining six merits will be enjoyed by the living. Therefore, in the present and the future, good men and women who hear this should try their best to practice and then enjoy their full merits. That evil impermanence comes without appointment, their consciousness is confused, they do not know the blessings of sin. Within 49 days, like a stupid person or a deaf person, or staying in offices to discuss karma, after the evaluation is complete, you should follow karma and receive retribution. While not sure what to do, you will have to endure countless sufferings, not to mention falling into other evil paths. People who die before they are born, within forty-nine days, every minute and every second, expect their loved ones to cultivate blessings and save them. During this time, they will accept retribution according to karma. If you are a sinner, after thousands of lifetimes, there will be no day of liberation. If one commits the five sins without interruption, one must fall into the great hell, experiencing thousands of lifetimes, ten thousand lifetimes, forever suffering pain and suffering."
"When a person is about to die, if there is a relative in the house, even if there is only one person, who recites the Buddha's name loudly for the sick person, that person, in addition to the five innocent sins, will have all other karmas destroyed. The five innocent sins, even though they are extremely serious, can go through countless lifetimes and cannot be escaped. But at the time of death, someone else recites the Buddha's name on their behalf, and those sins are gradually eliminated. What's more, he confesses himself. Gain immeasurable blessings, destroy countless sins."
Please, those of you who have not read the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Vow to Merit Sutra, please definitely get a copy to read carefully and learn. If you can get a copy of the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra explained by Venerable Master Hsuan Hua, it will be easier to understand. Before and after your loved ones' death and burial, only chanting sutras and reciting Buddha's name for them can help them be born on the path of goodness. Using the flesh of living beings to worship ghosts or eating the flesh of living beings during the funeral will increase the karma of the deceased. It is best to abstain from meat and alcohol within 49 days, at least abstain from alcohol, meat, onions, garlic, chives and eggs on the days of the funeral. All family members or groups of relatives should chant the Ksitigarbha sutras to the deceased, at least once a day, an unlimited number of times, and the remaining time recite Namo Amitabha Buddha continuously. Use the Buddha chanting machine to lead the chanting, the more people chanting along, the better.
When reading sutras or reciting Buddha's name, your mind must focus on the sutra text or Buddha's name, and in your heart you must have the idea: "Reciting Buddha, chanting sutras to wish the deceased to be reborn in the realm of Ultimate Bliss". If the mouth chants sutras, chants Buddha, but the mind is often scattered (not sincere), then the deceased will not receive maximum benefit.
Then, every time you come to a retreat (7 days), recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra 3 to 7 times in front of the Buddha statue at home (you can place a tablet or photo of the deceased next to the Buddha statue), either by one person or by many people. Relatives who are not convenient to come to the deceased's house to chant, can chant the sutras in front of the Buddha statue at their home (whether there is a tablet or not), just before chanting the sutras, or reciting the Buddha, or reciting the Great Compassion Mantra (21 times or 49 times) say a sentence to recite for the deceased, praying for Buddha's blessings to be born into Ultimate Bliss.
If you truly follow the above requirements and chant sutras and chant Buddha deliverance for the deceased, the deceased will certainly receive great benefits. If the deceased while still alive was the one observing the precepts reciting Buddha's name (no matter how short or long the time observing the precepts was), he will definitely be reborn in the realm of Ultimate Bliss. If one is not observing the precepts while still alive, one will certainly be born into heaven or become a human again. If relatives chanting sutras do not observe the precepts, the deceased will not receive great benefits, but will certainly not fall into the three evil paths.
Gods, Asuras and humans are the three good paths. Animals, hungry ghosts, and hell are the three evil paths. Within 49 days, killing and eating meat will increase the karma of the deceased. Things like sewing mourning clothes, burning paper money, and using lots of expensive wreaths and flower baskets... Not only does it not help the deceased, but it also dissipates their good fortune, like spending their money in the next life. Therefore, showing respect to the elderly should be done while they are alive, not after they have died.
The Ksitigarbha Sutra says: “When dying, parents and relatives should create blessings, to support the deceased, they can hang flags, oil lamps, or read prayers, make offerings of Buddha statues, statues of saints, chant the names of Buddha, Bodhisattva, and Bich Chi Buddha to make a title, each title reaches the dying person's ears, or is heard in their consciousness. These sentient beings, due to evil karma, would definitely fall into evil paths, but thanks to relatives who bless them at the end of their lives, all sins are destroyed. If you can create many good deeds in the forty-nine days after death, it will help those sentient beings forever leave the evil path, be born in the heavenly and human realms, enjoy supreme joy, and present relatives will also receive immeasurable benefits.
The person who has just passed away, "for 49 days, every minute and every second, waits for relatives to create blessings to save them. After this time, just follow karma and receive retribution." Therefore, relatives of the deceased, within 49 days, should recite Buddha and chanting sutras a lot, that is the greatest help for the deceased.
In the wrong way of organizing a funeral, the deceased's consciousness (called the soul) will be very angry with relatives, but yin and yang are separate, they can see and hear everything the family says and does, and also know each person's thoughts, but cannot communicate with the family. If the deceased person had any conflicts with you while they were alive, if you have anything wrong with them, as long as you sincerely recite the Buddha and chant the sutras for them, not only will the resentment between you and them be resolved, but the deceased will also appreciate you. Therefore, filial children should study the Ksitigarbha Sutra and reform wrong funeral customs. That is a wise action to benefit the deceased, benefit the living, and benefit the nation and people.

tieu_de: FRANCE DOES NOT HAVE HIGH SCHOOLS, ALL SUBJECTS ARE HIGH SCHOOLS
tom_tat: Ask: The meaning of practicing meditation is so profound, my fellow practitioner said that only practicing Pure Land and reciting Buddha's name is the fastest and most convenient. Moreover, it can bring karma (bring karma) rebirth. Zen school is for people with physical base...
noi_dung:
Ask: The meaning of practicing meditation is so profound, my fellow practitioner said that only practicing Pure Land reciting Buddha's name is the fastest and most convenient. Moreover, it can achieve karma (bring karma) rebirth. Zen school is for people with superior ability to practice. So what dharma should I practice?
Answer: My point of view is that, if you cannot strictly maintain precepts and repentance of the evil karmas created in this life and never repeat them, then no matter how many Buddha's names you chant or chant sutra texts every day, you are only married to Buddha and cannot go beyond the Three Realms. In the future, when you gain a human body again, you will still have the opportunity to be close to Buddha's teachings, that's all.
"Body of karma" refers to karma from a previous life. Only when one can repentance of karma sins in this life, and never commit them again, can one bring the previous life's karma to rebirth. In the "Four strains of pure repentance" it is said: "If you light a lamp on your body, or burn a finger, or burn a piece of incense on your body, then I say to those people, all debts from time immemorial until now will be paid off in one moment." This refers to previous karma, absolutely not to say that after lighting a lamp, burning fingers, burning incense and creating karma again, one can also bring rebirth karma.
Think about it, a person in this life only knows how to recite Buddha's name but cannot get rid of killing, religion, lust, delusion, and alcohol. He cannot practice the ten good karmas. Karma in this life has not been paid off yet. How can there be one?
Can I carry karma from previous generations? People who practice Zen school are also people who recite Buddha's name, like the high-ranking monks in Zen school such as Venerable Hu Van, the eternal Zen school Patriarchs all have pictures and paintings holding rosaries, eyes half-closed, chanting without leaving the Buddha's name. Sitting cross-legged in meditation is a method of purifying the mind. "meditation" means quiet meditation, calmly thinking about the karma sins you have committed in the ten evil karmas, sincerely repentance, in Buddha's mind dedicating merit to the sentient beings you have hurt, forever not re-offending, both repentance of karma sins, and eliminating negative thoughts. This is a good method of meditation. Just use your mind to be single-minded and not distracted, and be sincere to the extreme. You will naturally feel the shock of heaven and earth, and there will be a time when "the dark willow flowers brighten the whole village" (Mountains and water are at the end of their minds/The shadow of fresh willow flowers is a village).
Thinking about the sentence "who recites Buddha" is to keep your mind at the moment before this sentence is recited - the place of no thought, and prolong it indefinitely. In a place where there is mindfulness (when thinking about the original face of the person chanting the Buddha) but without thoughts, like a cat stalking a mouse, it can always be the time of enlightenment. When you practice successfully, you will personally feel the magic in it, "eat your own food and be full yourself" This realm cannot be described in words, having such concentration, enlightenment is immediately before your eyes.
Reciting Buddha is also a method of calming the mind, using one recitation of Buddha to replace other distracting thoughts. When the thought runs away, it is pulled back to continue reciting. Over time, reciting Buddha becomes fragments, chains, until there is no longer anyone or self, that is, when reciting Buddha Samadhi wisdom appears - reciting Buddha is also meditation.
Meditation and reciting the Buddha's name are both methods to clean one's own mind, they are both methods of purifying the mind,
One is not two, it is two but not two. Although the methods for enlightenment and approach are different, the goal is the same. If you feel that any method is suitable for you, which method is effective, then choose that method. Once you have chosen a method, persevere with it. Don't change methods because you can't see the realm for three days. One way in the morning and another in the afternoon. It's like standing at a crossroads, not knowing which road leads to Chang'an, going East and then turning back, going West and then doubting, then you will never reach Chang'an. "The Dharma is not high or low, every method is the best", the method that suits you is the best method.
Practicing is about correcting our wrong actions and words, whether it's meditation or reciting the Buddha's name, these are methods to help you attain wisdom and support. The most important thing is still observing the precepts and practicing the ten good karmas. If you are truly determined to do this and keep it for a long time, you will have achieved the Way. All Buddhas Bodhisattva are happy, the Heavenly Dragons and Eightfold Family of Dharma Protectors respect you, and you are greatly supported by the Way. One day, you will have wisdom appear in a single thought, thanks to Buddha Bodhisattva blessing you.
Over the past ten years, along with Venerable Dieu Phap, I have met dozens of people who sincerely observed the precepts of cultivating goodness. Thanks to the enlightenment of Venerable Dieu Phap, in one thought they were able to attain the five eyes and six powers, each with its own characteristics. They do not engage in meditation, nor do they recite Buddha's name non-stop, but just steadfastly observe the precepts of cultivating goodness, when the time comes, someone will naturally come to cultivate (including Buddha Bodhisattva in the dream of enlightenment).
Once wisdom appears, ignorance is self-destructed, leaving the Three Realms is a natural thing. If you don't observe the precepts, don't eliminate the ten evils, just rely on meditation and you will gain some evil
If you are wise, you will lose your path and less supporting conditions. Soon your happiness will run out and your wisdom will be gone. When you die, you will definitely fall into hell.
If one can not only believe in Buddha's teachings, but also begin to observe the precepts, that person has superior capacity. After many times others have advised me to study Buddha and return to the right path, that person is also of superior ability. As long as you are diligent and don't give up, you can definitely achieve success in this life. In the "Four Kinds of Pure Repentance" it is said that prostitutes, widows, adulterers, thieves, and butchers can all be the reincarnation of Bodhisattva Arhats. They are just ignorant and have not yet enlightened. Once they turn around, they will definitely have achievements.
Enlightenment, wisdom, is not something that can be practiced, but something that can be cultivated. "Diligence in the practice of precepts, concentration and wisdom", must "extinguish greed, anger and ignorance". Regardless of any sect, without these ten words, one cannot achieve Buddhahood. These ten words are also the ticket to the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

tieu_de: meditation AND Pure Land
tom_tat: Ask: In Buddhism, it is said that meditation master Vinh Minh Dien Tho is the reincarnation of Amitabha Buddha. He left behind the Four Teachings, which said: "With meditation without Pure Land, nine out of ten people go wrong." He is the one...
noi_dung:
Ask: In Buddhism, it is said that meditation master Vinh Minh Dien Tho is the reincarnation of Amitabha Buddha. He left behind the Four Teachings, which said: "With meditation without Pure Land, nine out of ten people go wrong." He is a member of the meditation lineage but said meditation is not equal to Pure Land, what do you understand about this sentence?
Answer: The complete verse is: "1. Is there meditation? Pure Land Ten people, nine lost their way. Warm scene when appearing
Blink and follow it.
Later became Buddha, Patriarch.
No meditation, no Pure Land Iron beds, bronze pillars of fire! For thousands of lifetimes, there will be no place to rely on."
When the World-Honored One was still alive, there was only Buddha teaching, in the teaching there was no sect or sect. After the World-Honored One entered Nirvana, along with the widespread spread of Buddha's teachings and different methods of practice, there was gradually a division into Mahayana and Hinayana, or called Southern Buddhism and Northern Buddhism, along with five major sects: meditation, Doctrine, Vinaya, Tantra, and Purity with different practice methods. Even though divided into five tones, the purpose is still the same, that is: Eliminate false thoughts and attachments, attain Buddhahood.
"The three worlds are only mind, all dharmas are only consciousness". meditation, Teachings, Vinaya, Tantra, and Purity all take purifying the mind as the goal, taking observing the precepts as the basis, with no distinction between high, low, noble, and low. The two words "Pure Land" refer to a pure mind, not just the Pure Land theme. The Pure Land sect uses reciting the Buddha's name as a method to stop delusions, and is also a common method to "stop delusions and prevent delusions" (stop false thoughts, prevent delusions) of other sects. As for sitting meditation, it is another method that helps Zen school disciples open the wisdom of "clear mind and see nature" on the basis of reciting Buddha. Patriarch Dat Ma said: "Buddha is mind, mind is Buddha, Buddha is religion, religion is meditation". Therefore, meditation and meditation, along with other sects, are brothers of the same origin, so why do they distinguish between high, low, noble and low?
Regarding the Four Teachings of meditation master Vinh Minh Dien Tho, considering the phenomenon at that time and now, it is completely correct. I understand as follows:
"Is there meditation? Pure Land Ten people, nine lost their way. Warm scene when appearing
Currently, many people participate in meditation, over time, it is no longer the same as the period of "Nanh Hoa Vi Tieu" until the period of Patriarch Dharma Faced with Cliffs. There are more and more people who practice meditation without concentration. They only learn to meditate without cultivating their minds. Most of them are looking outward. Just satisfied with achieving a little "pure" and "peaceful" realm. Or if you feel a little light, you will consider yourself diligent and "enlightened". It is impossible to take another step on a hundred meter tall column. And this type of "elaboration" is only the realm of the first stage of meditation, is "warm realm", and is not ultimate. If you follow the skandhas (five skandhas), you will lose the right path and go down the wrong path. That is not meditation. If you don't adjust in time, you will "wink at it" and go down a wrong path. It's all due to not cultivating the mind internally, the mind is focused outwardly, so "out of ten people, nine are on the wrong path".
Therefore, just knowing how to meditate without purifying the mind is not useful and cannot be called meditation.
“Without meditation, there is Pure Land. All cultivators can escape suffering. rebirth sees Amitabha Lo without enlightenment.”
People who do not like to meditate or participate in meditation but know how to pray internally, "tolerate what others cannot endure, do what others cannot do, do things for others, succeed for others", often sit quietly thinking about their own mistakes, avoid discussing the mistakes of others... Such practitioners have seen Amitabha's self-nature, and will definitely be reborn in Ultimate Bliss in the future, so they are called "thousands of people practice and escape". If you only recite Buddha with your mouth without truly practicing, even if you recite until your throat becomes hoarse, it will be useless. In the end, you will not meet Amitabha.
“If there is meditation, there is Pure Land, like a tiger adding horns”, the tiger is already majestic, if two more horns are added, wouldn't it be even more powerful and powerful, and it will definitely be achieved. Being a teacher and Buddha, this is obvious! This is the practice method that meditation master Vinh Minh Dien Tho praises. Otherwise, why would he use the image of a tiger with horns to compare it to "meditation plus tranquility"?
As for those who do not have good roots, they do not practice meditation nor recite the Buddha's name. Living a life of confusion, wasting one time in the human world, naturally losing one's human body, "for thousands of lifetimes and thousands of lives, with no one to rely on".

tieu_de: DRINK ALCOHOL, EAT MEAT AND GO TO NIFIM
tom_tat: Ask: In the area where we live, there are a number of lay people who often go to pray for the deceased, help those who are reborn, or organize dharma conferences. But I know there are many people among them who eat meat and fish, so the chanting is effective...
noi_dung:
Ask: In the area where we live, there are a number of lay people who often go to pray for the deceased, help those who are reborn, or organize dharma conferences. But I know that many of them eat meat and fish, so is chanting effective?
Answer: Regarding the benefit of the Buddhas for the deceased, in the Ksitigarbha Sutra it is said: “If there is a man or woman who does not cultivate good deeds while alive, they commit many crimes. After death, if relatives, large and small, create welfare for them and do all the holy things for them, out of the seven merits, the deceased only gets one part, the remaining six merits belong to the living. Therefore, good men and good women in the present and future should listen and improve themselves, and practice each part for themselves to enjoy." Buddha in this sutra said that, when a mortal does not end the ten evil deeds while alive, does not practice the ten good deeds, and does not do great good deeds, then after death, his descendants and relatives want to create merit for them. For example, releasing animals, deliverance, or sponsoring charity activities,... Then of the seven parts of merit, the deceased only gains one part, the remaining six parts of merit are self-benefiting for the living. Why is that? Because cultivating merit depends on financial resources, after the death, the property in the house belongs to the living, and the living is willing to use their assets to cultivate merit for the deceased, then the merit is naturally greater than the deceased. Therefore Buddha hopes: "Good men and good women in the present and future should listen and improve themselves, enjoying each part for themselves."
Regarding the issue of people drinking alcohol and eating meat chanting sutras deliverance, Buddha in the Lankavatara Sutra said: “I see them all
born as your own child, how can you allow meat to be used as food, not even happy, let alone eating it yourself. Dai Hue! All kinds of onions, garlic, chives, palanquins, and hyacinths are smelly and unclean. They can block the Holy Path and also block the pure realm of humans and gods in this world, not to mention the Pure Land retribution of all Buddhas! Alcohol, too, hinders the Holy Path, can damage good karma, and cause many mistakes. Therefore Dai Hue! Those who practice the Holy Path should not eat all kinds of these five spices that have a foul taste." It has been clearly stated here that a cultivator who drinks wine, eats meat, and eats the five spices, still finds it difficult to achieve the good results of humans and heavens, and wants to deliver to others the liberation of life and death, rebirth Pure Land, is even more difficult. But when a person is about to die, when he hears the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, a sound passes through his ears, he will never experience the suffering of the three evil paths. Therefore, if you want to deliver to others rebirth Pure Land, you must first purify your body and mind.
If you chant sutras and deliverance to others just to seek food, drink, or money from the deceased's family, that is sowing the seeds of hell. Step back from the abyss, it is not too late, the sins you have committed, quickly repentance before Buddha, absolutely do not commit them again. Buddha said, sins fill the sky, repentance immediately disappears, let alone the karma sins you create when you do not understand the reason.
In the second beatitude of the "Three Blisses" in the Infinite Life Buddha Sutra, the Buddha wants us to "keep all the precepts" and stop eating meat, which is an important content in the Mahayana Bodhisattva precepts. Without giving up eating meat, how can we talk about "keeping all the precepts"?
In the Pure Land Sutra, Buddha said, Pure Land dharma is "not Hinayana", it is Mahayana Buddha dharma, how can Mahayana Buddha disciples not follow Mahayana precepts?
In the conditions of the three levels of rebirth in the Infinite Life Sutra, there is one thing that is "creating Bodhi mind", how can there be a Bodhisattva who has Bodhi mind and still eats living beings?
Buddha in the "Four Medicine Dharma" points out that we should "follow the meaning, not rely on the nonsense", so true practitioners must rely on the meaning to give up meat, but should not use the unclear meaning of the three pure flesh as a reason to eat meat.

tieu_de: DFI TA Buddha, CAN Buddhist monks eat meat?
tom_tat: Ask: Some people say that Buddhists can eat meat, they say that "in Buddha's precepts, it is only forbidden to kill, not to eat meat", "when eating meat, you can eat the three pure flesh (three types of pure meat)". In the book Notes on modern cause and effect...
noi_dung:
Ask: Some people say that Buddhists can eat meat, they say that "in Buddha's precepts, it is only forbidden to kill, not to eat meat", "when eating meat, you can eat the three pure flesh (three types of pure meat)". In the book Notes on Modern Cause and Effect, he said that eating meat not only leads to unjust retribution in the future, but also causes many diseases in this life. So which statement is correct?
Answer: The stories in Notes on Modern Cause and Effect are a tiny fraction of the countless cases I have encountered. Moreover, for the past ten years, almost every day there have been cases before my eyes, the harmful effects of eating meat are very great, causing us countless sufferings.
The so-called being able to eat the three pure meats, which Buddha said is a means for those who have just believed in Buddha and cannot immediately give up eating meat, is explained in the Lankavatara Sutra Sutra (translated by Bodhi Liuzhi) about the order of gradually stopping eating meat. When a person constantly recites the Buddha, chants sutras and understands reason, he will naturally give up eating meat completely. It is like advising a person who smokes two packs of cigarettes a day to quit smoking. It is impossible to immediately stop completely. First, advise him to smoke one pack a day, then half a pack, then only smoke one cigarette after meals, and then quit completely. Of course, there are also people who are determined to immediately quit smoking, alcohol, and meat. This is the action of a Mahayana practitioner. In the Mahayana Sutra of Entering the Lankavatara (translated by Thuc Xoa Nanda), it says: Bo
Having compassion for all living beings, like yourself, how can you see them and think of eating them?
Prince Siddhartha, as the crown prince, gave up glory and wealth to practice asceticism, until he sat under the Bodhi tree and enlightened, becoming Shakyamuni Buddha Buddha. He was the only one in the whole world. Why did so many people learn to follow him later? Because the Dharma he preached is the truth of the universe, this has been proven for nearly three thousand years. Not eating the flesh of living beings has been affirmed by the World-Honored One for a long time. It was absolutely not until it was transmitted to China that it was proposed by Emperor Wu of Liang. In the "Four Pure and Clear Repentance Sutras" of the Shurangama Sutra and the Shurangama Sutra - "Precepts of fleshly foods" clearly explains why it is forbidden to eat the flesh of living beings, and why the Buddha's disciples when the Buddha was still alive could eat five types of pure meat. If today someone says "Buddha didn't say don't eat meat", it's most likely because they don't understand the Buddha's scriptures. For the convenience of readers, I would like to quote a passage of Buddha's teachings in "The Four Pure and Clear Repentance" as follows:
“Anan, in other worlds, all sentient beings in the six paths, if the mind does not kill, will not follow the continuum of birth and death. He practiced Samadhi, originally to escape from the world of suffering. If he did not eliminate the mind of killing, he could not escape from the world of trouble. Even though there is a lot of wisdom and meditation present, if you do not eliminate killing, you will definitely fall into Shinto. High-ranking people will become powerful demons, middle-ranking people will become yakshas and ghost commanders flying in the night. Low-class people will become rakshasas walking on the ground. These ghosts and gods also have followers, each claiming to have achieved the supreme path. After my nirvana, in the Dharma Ending Age, there will be many such ghosts and spirits, spreading throughout the world, claiming that eating meat can achieve Bodhi. A Nan ! I allow the Bhikkhus to eat five meals
pure flesh; That flesh was created by My divine power and has no life base. Your Brahmanical land is hot, humid, and has gravel, so vegetables cannot survive; Therefore, I bless you with the power of great compassion, and through great compassion I call it meat so that you can have a taste. How can those who eat living beings be called Buddha's disciples after the Tathagata's nirvana? You must know: Those who eat meat, even if their minds are opened like Tam-ma-di, are just Great Rakshasas, and when the end comes, they will have to suffer in the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death, and are not disciples of the Buddha. People like that kill each other, cannibalize each other, and devour each other endlessly. How can they get out of the Three Realms? So he taught people to practice the Samadhi dharma, and then to stop killing. That is the second decisive instruction on the purity of the Tathagata and all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones of the past. Therefore, Ananda, if one practices meditation but does not stop killing, it is like covering one's ears and shouting loudly while praying that others will not hear; That's called 'wanting to hide but becoming obvious'. The Bodhisattva monks and the pure Bhikkhus, when walking on the path, do not even step on living grass, let alone pull it with their hands, so why would someone with great compassion take the flesh and blood of living beings as food? Those Bhikkhus who do not use cotton, Oriental silk, leather boots, leather shoes, leather coats, fur coats, milk, cheese, and condensed milk of that region, then those Bhikkhus will truly be liberated in life; After paying their debt first, they will not return to the Three Realms again. Why? Because serving their bodies is creating conditions for them, just like a person who eats rice from the ground never leaves the ground. Whoever can make his body and mind stay away from the body and body of all living beings, and neither body nor mind wear or eat them, then I say that he is a true liberator. As I say, this is what Buddha said; If you don't say so, it means Ma Ba Tuan's words."
Buddha used divine power to manifest "five types of pure meat" (compared to three types of pure meat - not seeing the kill, not hearing the sound when being killed, not killing for oneself, plus dying on their own, half-eaten animals), because at that time in India the weather was hot, the soil was often wet, there was a lot of sand and rocks, grass and vegetables could not grow, and the animals that appeared had no life base, temporarily called meat, but were in fact not real meat. Just like Sun Wukong in Journey to the West used feathers to transform into an incarnation of Sun Wukong, not a body with a life base.
In the Lotus Sutra, if you want to manifest, you only need to manifest in a single thought. In the Amitabha Sutra, birds can also manifest. Therefore, in ancient times with special conditions, there was Buddha in the world, Sangha appeared, in natural conditions where meat could not be given up, Buddha reluctantly used divine power to manifest lifeless animals. After Buddha's Nirvana, Buddhism spread throughout the world. There have long been no more animals manifested by Buddha's divine power. Why do we still use the excuse that during Buddha's time in this world, people gave us whatever they ate, to destroy the precepts that Buddha set up at that time? Buddha in the Brahma Net Sutra told his disciples: There are ten Bodhisattva precepts. Among them, the precept of killing is the first: “Buddha said, if you are a Buddha disciple, whether you kill yourself, teach others to kill, create conditions to kill, praise killing, see killing and rejoice, even curse killing, cause of killing, cause of killing, dharma of killing, karma of killing, up to all living beings, do not intentionally kill. Bodhisattva must develop a permanent mind of compassion, filial piety, and help all sentient beings, but on the contrary, he voluntarily kills for pleasure, which is Bodhisattva's Paramita sin.
Do not eat the flesh of living beings. People who eat meat will cut off the seeds of great compassion and Buddha nature. All living beings seeing this will leave, so all Bodhisattva must not eat the flesh of living beings. Eating meat will commit countless sins.
Look at the story in the Ksitigarbha Sutra about the mother of the girl Light Eye. Just because "I love eating fish and turtles, I also eat their babies, fried or cooked, whatever you want. Calculating the number of lives eaten, it must be millions of times", that's why she fell into evil.
No need to give any more examples. Saying that “Buddha did not teach us not to eat meat” is a complete lie. The Venerable Patriarchs from past to present have all said that we must "penetrate the scriptures, wisdom like the ocean". The thirteenth patriarch of the Pure Land sect, Great Master An Quang, also advised us to "taboo eating meat" (see details in An Quang Great Master Van Sao). In this day and age, reading the Shurangama Sutra is urgent, especially the sections "Four types of pure repentance" and "Fifty types of skandhas". The Sutra Entering the Lankavatara - "Chapter on the preparation of fleshly food" and the Brahma Hammock Sutra should also be read many times to deeply understand. Thanks to that, we will be able to distinguish between right and wrong. As for those who propagate that Buddha and his disciples also eat meat, as said in the Lankavatara Sutra, that person will "fall into a place of no benefit, without saints, unable to hear the Dharma, nor meet current and future sage disciples, let alone meet all Buddhas Tathagata."

tieu_de: MEANING OF VIFIC DONG TÇN HUÄNG
tom_tat: Ask: In "The Four Pure Kinds of Minh Repentance", there is a passage as follows: "After I pass away, if there are any Bhikkhus who have made up their minds and decided to practice the Samadhi dharma, and can light a lamp in front of the Tathagata's statue,...
noi_dung:
Ask: In "The Four Pure Kinds of Minh Repentance", there is a passage as follows: "After my passing away, if there are any Bhikkhus who are determined to practice the Samadhi dharma, and can light a lamp in front of the Tathagata's image, or burn a finger, or light a piece of incense on their body, then I say that those people will pay off all their debts from beginningless time until now, completely separate from the world and forever be free from the defilements, although they do not immediately understand the path of Supreme Enlightenment, but their mind They have already decided on the dharma. If we do not create such a cause of self-sacrifice, then even if we cultivate to Vo Vi, we will still have to return to be born as a human being to pay off our old debt, just like I have to eat rice and horses." What does this sutra text mean?
Answer: The Buddha preached this sutra text, as I understand it: Buddha said that after he entered Nirvana, if there is a Bhikkhu (Buddhist practitioner) who is determined to practice to escape the Three Realms, this person can, if possible, in front of the Buddha statue, or burn a lamp on his body, or burn a knuckle, or burn an incense stick on his body, these three methods can choose one depending on his circumstances. Why does Buddha advise us to do so? Because from beginningless eons until now, we have owed immeasurable debt, and by enduring this small pain, we can pay off all of that debt. Will never have to be reborn in this Saha world to endure suffering anymore, forever free from all defilements. Even though one has not immediately attained the enlightenment path of Buddhahood, this person, on the path of learning Buddha Dharma, will never be regressed.
mind, fall. If you don't have the heart to sacrifice yourself to pay your debt like that, then even if you practice to reach the high realm of Buddha, you will definitely have to return to being a human because the debt from previous lives has not been paid off. This is like the Buddha who ate horse barley for ninety days.
The Buddha in a previous life was a Pham Chi (a person leaving the home life who practices paganism), leading five hundred disciples to practice on Pham Chi mountain. At that time, there was also a living Buddha. One time, the Buddha went to beg for alms, because in the ashram there was a Bhikkhu who was sick and could not go out to beg for alms. He told another Bhikkhu to ask for an extra portion of vegetarian rice to bring back for the sick Bhikkhu to eat. When this Bhikkhu brought rice over Pham Chi mountain, Pham Chi smelled the fragrance of the rice, immediately became jealous and said: "Why do these bald monks eat such delicious things? They only deserve to eat horse barley." His disciple heard what his teacher said, also agreed and said: "Yes, they should have eaten barley meant for horses." Pham Chi later practiced to become a Buddha, that is, Shakyamuni Buddha. Once, Shakyamuni Buddha led five hundred disciples to a country for a summer retreat. The king initially welcomed it, but then stopped making offerings. At that time, a horse herder saw that the Buddha and his five hundred disciples had nothing to eat, so he used barley for the horses to make offerings to the Buddha and his five hundred disciples. These five hundred disciples are five hundred Arhats, also five hundred young disciples who followed Master Pham Chi to practice in the past. Even though they had all attained fruition, because in their previous lives they had slandered "these bald monks are only worthy of eating horse barley", so they had to eat horse barley for ninety days. If a person is determined to practice to escape the Three Realms and become Buddha, but does not choose one of the three methods of burning a lamp, burning fingers, or burning incense sticks to
If you sacrifice your life to pay off your debt, even if you become a Buddha in the future, you will be like a Buddha and have to pay off your previous life's debt. In the scriptures, it is also said that Shakyamuni Buddha had a headache for three days, also because in his previous life when he was a child, he hit a fish three times on the head.
Buddha preached these stories as just a manifestation, to remind us that Buddha's divine power cannot overcome karma. The reason is "Suppose that in hundreds of thousands of lives, the karma created is not lost", only sincere repentance can eliminate sins in this life, and debts from beginningless previous lives must rely on the method that Buddha taught to completely eliminate them. Don't think that just by studying Buddha and having Buddha's protection, you can do wrong without suffering retribution, and then you can rest assured and not worry.
After becoming Buddha, Shakyamuni Buddha gained supreme wisdom and knew how to help his disciples pay off debts from previous lives by the method of 'paying off karma' only once, with the hope that we will soon achieve the path to Buddhahood. This is Buddha's compassion and concern for us.
From here, I also thought about why people leaving the home life in China burn tons of incense on top of their heads. This is because the Patriarchs clearly understood the meaning of burning incense, so they encouraged the Sangha to do this. That's why there are lay people who understand this meaning and burn incense sticks on their arms or legs, or even burn a knuckle. I once met a male layperson at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas in America who had burned a knuckle on his little finger. He said he didn't feel any pain at the time of the burn, but the next day the pain was unbearable and he had to take painkillers. Meanwhile, lay people who burned tons of incense on their bodies said that they did not feel any pain
Their method is to use a little ripe banana and mash it, about the size of a pea, stick it on your hand or foot, then insert the burned incense tip (only the red flame remains) about an inch into the banana. When the incense burns out, there is no need to do anything else, just feel hot, not painful, and no need to apply medicine. Just be careful not to get infected, after a day or two blisters will appear, then quickly disappear and leave scars. I've heard stories from lay people who have burned incense sticks, but I haven't practiced it myself. I write here just to let fellow practitioners understand that burning incense is not a 'cruel' act. Lighting a lamp on the body, burning a knuckle or burning an incense stick is for Bhikkhus leaving the home life, not something that lay disciples are required to do. Burning or not burning is up to each person's decision. I see many lay people have chosen to burn incense on their hands or feet, they don't say it and no one sees it, but old karma can be eliminated, new karma is not created, and rebirth in the realm of Ultimate Bliss, flowers blooming to see Buddha is certain without doubt.
Venerable Master Hsuan Hua taught: “In Buddhism, all scriptures are very important, but the Shurangama Sutra is the most important. Wherever there is the Shurangama Sutra, that place is where the Dharma still exists. When the Shurangama Sutra no longer exists, it is a sign of the end of the Dharma. The Shurangama Sutra is Buddha's true body, Buddha's relics, and Buddha's temple tower. All Buddhists need to devote all their strength and enthusiasm to protect this Shurangama Sutra."

tieu_de: MIRACULOUS Dharma Ç IN THE SUTRAS
tom_tat:
chanting sutras must be understood for their meaning, not recited for quantity. One evening, the Venerable Dieu Phap lectured on the Sutra.
Ksitigarbha to lay people at a location in Henan. When he preached the passage: "If there are sentient beings who steal wealth...
noi_dung:
chanting sutras must be understood for their meaning, not recited for quantity. One evening, the Venerable Dieu Phap lectured on the Sutra.
Ksitigarbha to lay people at a location in Henan. When he preached the passage: "If there is a living being who steals the property of the permanent residence, food, food, clothes, even a small thing without permission, they will fall into the endless hell, going through tens of thousands of eons without an expiration date," the old Venerable said: "What is 'an object that is not allowed to be taken'? Any item in the temple that is taken away without the consent of the temple, including a plant or a tree branch, will cause that person to fall into the endless hell."
At this time, a female layperson in her 40s suddenly asked worriedly: "I have a very good relationship with the abbot of a temple. I've been making offerings for her for many years, and we have a very close relationship. Sometimes, when I go to the abbot's room and she's not there, I feel as comfortable as at home. If you see beads or small Buddha statues that you like, you can easily put them in your pocket. After all, those items were offered by others, and sooner or later the abbot would give them to others to tie the knot. Since you and the abbot are so close, of course 'the water closest to the tank benefits first'! So does this count as theft?
Old Venerable Dieu Phap replied: "Subjectively speaking, I had no intention of stealing, but these items were not given to me by the abbot. Not giving but taking, what do you say is that behavior?" The laywoman looked very worried, then said:
"Last year, in the temple's flower garden there were some very beautiful flowers. I decided that when the flowers produce seeds, I will take some seeds to plant at home. But when I wanted to get the seed, there was only one seed left, the others had been taken by someone else. When I put that flower seed in my bag, I also thought that next year this flower garden would no longer have that type of flower, it would be difficult to find. So taking one of these flower seeds is still considered theft? The Venerable smiled and asked again: "What do you think?
But you don't need to worry too much or be afraid. I have read the Ksitigarbha Sutra many times, but do not understand the meaning of the sutra, have no wisdom, and on the contrary, create karma. But thanks to you chanting sutras, today I understand the truth. „Great sins fill the sky, once repentance will be eliminated‟. Repentance before Buddha, don't do it again. If you still keep any of the items you took, return it to the abbot and admit your mistake directly. As for flower seeds, when the flowers form seeds again, give some back to the temple to plant, or even make offerings of some other types of flowers, all karma obstacles will be eliminated. If you can explain these principles to other Dharma friends, that is immeasurable merit!". The Venerable's words helped the laywoman feel at ease again.
The monk continued to teach: "We chant sutras first of all to understand the morality. When you understand morality, you will have wisdom, and will know that the tribulations you encounter are all due to bad causes you have sown in the past. Therefore, you must soon put an end to those bad causes and not sow new evil seeds. The rest depends on your own diligence in reciting Buddha, chanting sutras, repentance, and bringing that dedicating merit to sentient beings. This will help the evil seeds that you have sown in the past but have not yet germinated to gradually wither and dissipate. To achieve this goal, you must be a man or woman who keeps the five precepts and practices the ten good deeds. There are only good men and good women
chanting sutras, reciting Buddha's name and dedicating merit to sentient beings, only then can one gain great merit. Why is that? Because when you use pure body, speech, and mind to recite 'Namo Amitabha Buddha',
'Namo Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva', not only represents your sincere intention to take refuge in Buddha Bodhisattva, but also has the effect of calling sentient beings to take refuge in Buddha Bodhisattva. Your sincere heart will immediately respond to the Buddha, and the Buddha Light will shine on your body."
"A lot of people who recite Buddha's name ask me that when they recite Buddha's name, they feel a tingling, warm feeling from head to toe. What is that? I said it was Buddha's inspiration when he heard me chant his name, sending light to bless me, helping me eliminate past sins. At this time, around you, in heaven and on earth, there are many beings that you cannot see such as heavenly fairies, earth gods, hungry ghosts, wandering ghosts, seeing the wonderful impact when you recite Buddha, they will also recite Buddha. And when they chant Buddha, each person will immediately receive Buddha's blessings for sublimation and liberation. For example, people who die from explosions, cuts or cuts, ghosts with missing limbs, lonely souls who die from drowning, hanging, poisoning, car accidents or other sudden deaths, souls who cannot be reincarnated or have to wait a year to find a substitute karma to reincarnate, as long as they chant the Buddha's name, their bodies will immediately recover, lonely souls will immediately be reincarnated. And the longer the chanting time, the greater the benefit. Maybe at that time there will be hundreds, thousands, or even countless sentient beings who will benefit, including the plants, flowers, and animals around you. The number of sentient beings who benefit depends on the practice of the deep or shallow person.
For example, in 1994, I saw a giant tree in front of the yard of Pho Te Pagoda on Putuo Mountain suddenly turn into a human shape,
He knelt down with his hands clasped and asked me to explain the meaning of the sutra passage "The Path of Non-Suffering and the Extinction of Non-Suffering" in the Prajnaparamita Heart Sutra. I asked it: “Where did you hear the Prajnaparamita Sutra?” It says: “Venerable Master Hsuan Hua has just finished preaching the Heart Sutra at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas in America, but I still don't understand clearly the sentence 'The practice of non-suffering destroys the path', I hope the Venerable will teach me.” I asked: “Venerable Master Hsuan Hua preaches sutras in America, how come you can hear it at Putuo Mountain?”. The great tree said: “When Venerable Master Hsuan Hua preaches the sutra, all the dharma realms of space can hear it.”
"We do not have the same merit and magical power as Venerable Master Hsuan Hua, but in the area around you, or in the city or village where you reside, all sentient beings in heaven and earth benefit from your reciting the Buddha, chanting sutras. Therefore, people who chant Buddha must observe the precepts, purify their body, speech, and mind. Thus, not only will you enjoy countless benefits for yourself, but you will also benefit other sentient beings. Your natural merit will be great, enough to destroy your karma for many lifetimes. Every day reciting Buddha and chanting sutras brings immeasurable blessings and eliminates immeasurable sins."

tieu_de: IN THE Ksitigarbha Sutra, Kien Lao Divinity said to the Blessed One:
tom_tat: “I observe living beings in the past and future, when in my residence, in a clean place in the South, using soil, stone, bamboo, wood to build a shrine, a room, in which I can sculpt or use gold, silver, copper, iron to make...
noi_dung:
“I observe sentient beings in the past and future, when in my residence, in a clean place in the South, using soil, stone, bamboo, wood to build a shrine, a room, in which I can sculpt or use gold, silver, copper, iron to make Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva statues, burn incense making offerings, and worship and praise. This person will receive ten benefits at his residence. What are those benefits? Thứ nhất: fertile land; thứ hai: The house is always safe; thứ ba: deceased relatives are reborn in heaven; Wednesday: Those who are still alive have an increased lifespan; thứ năm: all wishes are fulfilled; thứ sáu: avoid
fires and floods; thứ bảy: eliminate all losses; thứ tám: prevent nightmares; thứ chín: Every entry and exit is protected by a spirit; thứ mười: often encounter holy causes...
The Earth Spirit again said to Buddha: World-Honored One! In the future, if there is a good man or good woman in his place of residence who keeps this sutra and a statue of Bodhisattva, and can also recite this sutra, making Bodhisattva offerings, I will use my supernatural powers to protect that person day and night, until floods, fires, robberies, disasters large and small are avoided, and all evil is destroyed."
The scriptures say very clearly that just by making offerings of Buddha statues, you can receive ten benefits. Think about it, if this person makes offerings of Buddha statues, worships and praises the Buddha, but is not filial to his parents, constantly kills and eats meat, and speaks evil and double-tongued words every day, can he receive "safety", "long life", "satisfaction", "guardianship when entering and exiting"? But "often encountering holy causes" is certain, because even though you are making offerings to Buddha but do not yet understand the principles, Buddha Bodhisattva will guide you to listen to the Dharma. Like today, among you, those who have given up eating meat, please raise your hand. (Out of a few dozen people, only three raised their hands. Among them, only one person, after believing in Buddha, gave up eating meat, another person did not eat pork, beef, or goat but still ate seafood, and another person was "a vegetarian from the womb" but did not know that onions, garlic, and chives should not be eaten). The Venerable said: “Observe the precepts, chant Buddha, chant Ksitigarbha sutras as mentioned above, practice persistently. You don't need to pray to Buddha, see if your illness is relieved or completely cured, and if your wish can be achieved. But take care that your wishes must not harm national interests or the interests of others. The scriptures say: “If in the future, there are good men and good women
Anyone who wants to wish for current and future wishes and events in large quantities of hundreds of thousands of millions, just needs to take refuge in worshiping, making offerings and praising the statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, then all wishes will be fulfilled.
In all three generations, all Buddhas did not lie, spoke the truth, told the truth, and did not lie. I hope that fellow practitioners will carefully study the Ksitigarbha Sutra and enjoy the benefits of the Dharma in practice. Finally, the Venerable Dieu Phap spoke a verse to end:
“Buddha in the heart is never far away. The wonderful dharma must be sought in the sutras and prayed for. The words are good medicine

tieu_de: DISCUSSION ABOUT SPIRITUAL POWERS
tom_tat: Ask: I have read Notes on modern cause and effect. In addition to understanding the principle of cause and effect, I am especially interested in the supernatural powers of the Venerable Dieu Phap. In the end, do magical powers come from practicing or cultivating...
noi_dung:
Ask: I have read Notes on modern cause and effect. In addition to understanding the principle of cause and effect, I am especially interested in the supernatural powers of the Venerable Dieu Phap. In the end, do magical powers come from practice or do they come from practice? If it is said that it comes from practicing, then many people who practice all their lives still do not have magical powers. If it is said that success comes from practice, then many people who practice do not have wisdom. But there really are people with supernatural powers, I always feel this is a mystery. Can you explain to us your knowledge in this field?
Answer: In the first modern Notes on Cause and Effect, I said that supernatural powers come from practice and cannot be obtained by asking. So why do many people practice all their lives but still do not have supernatural powers? "If you want to know the causes of previous lives, look at the results of this life; If you want to know the results of the next life, look at the cause of this life." This means that the appearance of supernatural powers in some people today is the result of practice from a previous life, or many previous lives, in the already existing nature, when the opportunity is ripe, it will naturally appear. It can appear when meditating and practicing qigong, it can appear when sitting still, or it can appear under the influence or suggestion of a certain external force, which is different for each person. Of course, there is also wisdom gained in this life. That is, if the previous life did not have the ability to penetrate the five eyes and six eyes, then in this life, if one can "suddenly enlighten" and open wisdom, it is also thanks to the "practice" of the previous life that in this life one can attain it. Modern people call it exploiting human potential, which is also true.
In "Four strains of pure repentance" of the Shurangama Sutra, Buddha said: "People who practice Samadhi are originally to get out of the world of dust, their lustful mind is not eliminated, they cannot get out of the world of dust. Even though there is a lot of wisdom and meditation present, if you don't eliminate lust, you will definitely fall into the devil's path... Even though there is a lot of wisdom and meditation present, if you don't eliminate the mind of killing, you will definitely fall into Shinto... Even though there is a lot of wisdom and meditation present, if you don't eliminate the mind of stealing, you will definitely fall into an evil path... Even though the body and mind are free from killing, religion, lust, and the three actions are perfect, but if one speaks with false language, the Tam-ma-ground will not be pure, will become a demon of love, and will lose the Tathagata's seed." Practitioners have "many wisdom", "present meditation" due to practicing Samadhi, but in the end, because they do not strictly adhere to the precepts, they do not achieve the right results, falling into the demon path, the Shinto path, and the evil path. After their life ends, they will continue to samsara back to the human world, changing heads to continue practicing. Once they encounter the opportunity as mentioned above, the wisdom from the previous life will reappear. If in this life you can grasp yourself, practice the right Dharma, and eliminate lust, killing, religion, and delusion, then in this life you will achieve enlightenment. If you have a little ability but are greedy for money, lust, fame and fortune, and even threaten and deceive others, then this person's meditation practice will no longer exist. Because if you gain the path (walking on the right path), you have a lot of support, but if you lose the path, you have less support. Heaven, earth, ghosts, and spirits no longer help you. Just like an old television, if the channel is not correct, or the antenna and tuning have problems, images and information cannot be received from the television station. You also can't "magically (television station)" anymore. If, because you once had a sweet taste, and now lose your magical powers and still pretend to have magical powers to defraud others of money, sooner or later you will be punished by the legal authorities, this has been proven through the outcome of many fraudulent "Great Masters" in society.
Therefore, observing the precepts and cultivating virtue is the basis of a spiritual practitioner. Having a little meditation practice, not everyone can necessarily preach the Dharma and preach the Sutras. This also depends on whether you have the ability to preach the Dharma and preach the Sutras or not and whether you have that mission or not. Like Venerable Dieu Phap, even people with deeper wisdom, they often hide in busy streets or deep mountains and forests, no different from ordinary people. When the time is not right, they will not reveal their talent. When the time comes, they will appear to educate sentient beings and complete their mission, then they will leave, or hide again.
If the disciple sent by the Demon King has some magical powers, he will begin to harm living beings. It is important to know that the Demon King's disciples, with the Demon King's help, have very strong magic power. Demons have a fighting mind, Buddhas have a compassionate mind. The only difference between demons and Buddhas is that they no longer have all the defilements. Demons easily bewitch sentient beings. They come to the human world and often appear with the appearance of "big ears, long earlobes", "white skin, healthy body" because when they practiced in their previous lives, they also planted blessings fields, but they just haven't eliminated all desires, so they fall into the demon path. Venerable Master Hsuan Hua says: "Wisdom appears, but it is also a big lie". The simple criterion to distinguish whether a person with supernatural powers is a Buddha disciple or one sent by the Demon King is to see whether he is greedy for money or not. If he is greedy for money, then it is fake. Disciples of the Demon King, because they had not practiced completely in their previous lives, they could not harmonize when teaching the Buddha Dharma. They often had many loopholes and contradictions, and could not justify themselves. They often praise themselves for achieving the ultimate path, like the "king of melon sellers", promoting themselves. If the person is leaving the home life, you can also see whether they keep their precepts or not, whether their actions, words, and posture have the four majesty or not. If you are a lay person, you talk a lot about food
Drinking, fame, non-stop smoking, drinking alcohol, eating meat, greed for money, lust, fame and fortune, eating and sleeping are not true Buddhists, unless you point it out to them and they can listen and change immediately.
Among those with supernatural powers, there are also some who are "soul possessed" mentioned in the Shurangama Sutra, among the fifty types of skandhas. The biggest characteristic of this type is not keeping precepts, relying on saying a few things about others to cheat money. This is not called magical power, but demonic power, created by ghosts and spirits possessing and entering the soul. They often say that they have seen a certain Buddha or Bodhisattva, and then the Buddha or Bodhisattva said something to them. All of these Buddha Bodhisattvas are manifested by Mara, thinking of themselves as saints. Not long after, the possessed ghosts and spirits feel discouraged and leave those people, and then they will no longer have any magical powers. As for evil people such as witches, fortune tellers, false gods and demons, greed for money, deceitful lust, and obvious evil spirits, they are even easier to identify.
In 1993, I met a factory director surnamed Ton, who talked with Venerable Dieu Phap for more than an hour, and then suddenly appeared miraculous powers. At that time, there was another person unfamiliar with Director Ton who also came to ask the Venerable for advice. Perhaps the Venerable wanted to educate both of them at the same time, so he smiled and asked Director Ton: "Do you know how many rooms his house has?"
Director Ton replied: "I don't know him, teacher."
Director Ton replied: "How is that possible? I don't have magical powers... Oh!..." Director Ton asked the other person in surprise:
"Your house has a total of six tiled houses, including the entrance, right?"
The other person was a little surprised and replied: "Yes, I guessed right." Hearing that, Director Ton seemed interested and confused.
The old Venerable said to the other person: "I want you to understand a principle: I don't want others to know unless I don't do it. Looks like you don't really believe it.
