Now, I understand that it's all caused by masturbation habits. Once the semen is drained, how can the body be good! At first, masturbation was only occasional, but as time passed and greed increased, the frequency became more and more intense, and the consequences also appeared like shadows and shapes.
After good high school karma, I did not pass the university entrance exam. My parents used money from my hard work to send me to a private university to study full-time and take the self-study exam. After graduating from university, my job was not favorable.
I can't find the job I want, even if I do, the salary won't be high. At this time, I began to "believe" in Buddha, but I completely did not understand Buddha's teachings, my belief was just superstition. I only know how to go to the temple to burn incense, bow to the Buddha, and pray for Buddha Bodhisattva's protection, but I don't know how to study Buddha and truly practice. As I got older, my parents naturally began to worry about my marriage, but even though I went on blind dates many times, nothing worked out. Because during my childhood, I lived in the midst of my parents' arguments and my relationship with my father was very tense, so I wanted to find someone with the same mindset as me to be my husband. So I went to the temple, bowed to the Buddha, burned incense and blindly prayed to Buddha and Bodhisattva for blessings.
Not long after, that person appeared, he did business elsewhere, even though my family reminded me that the distance was too far, we didn't understand each other well, the living environment was different... But I still think as long as he believes in Buddha, he is definitely a good person. Actually, whether it's good or bad, I don't even know. In the years that followed, I sacrificed a lot for this so-called "Buddha disciple", the bitterness could not be expressed in a few simple sentences, but in the end the result left me extremely disappointed. Before he met me, he had committed many years of adultery, even causing women to have abortions, and had a failed marriage.
Bodhisattva fears the cause, living beings fear the effect. It was that failed marriage that made him "believe" in Buddha and accept a qigong master as his teacher. From then on, he believed that the qigong master was the living Buddha and superstitiously propagated the things he did called Buddha dharma, which contained many absurdities. For example: The teacher did not let his disciples read the scriptures, saying that if they did not understand, they should not read; Some disciples came to see the teacher abroad, and the teacher said crazy things: "Whoever comes here to see me, will
attain Arhat immediately!". He used some magical powers to cure diseases, and there were many disciples throughout the country studying the qigong style he invented. As long as it's a health care product introduced by a teacher, everyone will rush to buy it. Some disciples are jealous because they compete with their master, or because they are greedy, they go to the teacher's company to work to make money.
If you sow bad causes, the results will naturally not be good. Finally, this qigong master, whom his disciples considered a living Buddha, fled to America around 1999. To date he has been married four times and has four sons. Domestic practitioners continue to produce and sell health care products, including physiological enhancement products. People who study the Dharma all understand that sexual enhancement products only increase lustful desires, which is a very serious sin! At that time, we both did not understand clearly, committed many sins of adultery, even created karma in the temple while burning incense at Putuo Mountain, and had an abortion once. But in the end we broke up, causing a lot of hurt to each other. The cause and effect of retribution is real and not false.
The reason for breaking up was that he continued to commit adultery outside, while I met the Dharma and took refuge in the Three Jewels, moving from superstition onto the path of learning true Buddha. I started chanting the Ksitigarbha sutras, repentance of evil karma, deeply believing in the true existence of cause and effect. I began to reflect on my behavior, and after a period of painful thinking, I chose to break up with him. (I need to explain clearly, actually it was not that Bodhisattva did not bless me to meet him, but because things gathered according to species, people divided into groups. I am still doing evil, how can I expect Bodhisattva to arrange a virtuous man for me? What qualifications do I have to have a good man as my husband? Everything is done by yourself, at your own risk!)
I read the book Notes on Modern Cause and Effect written by Master Qua Khanh while at his master's place, and was immediately fascinated by the cause and effect stories in the book. As if I had found a treasure, I read it in one sitting. Among them, the article "Discussion on Divine Power" touched me deeply. Isn't the ghost disciple that the book talks about the same person I met? The scriptures of Buddha Bodhisattva and the teachings of the wise man helped me have wisdom eyes, no longer confused or hesitant, and rationally broke up with him. Therefore, Buddhists must definitely read the sermon on the fifty types of negative demons and the "Four types of pure repentance" in the Shurangama Sutra! You will be deeply touched by the great wisdom of Shakyamuni Buddha, thereby increasing your own wisdom, and making accurate judgments and reasonable choices before people and phenomena in modern society!
Nowadays, there are quite a few men who have a decent appearance, style like a boss, have some money, speak skillfully, and even claim to believe in Buddha. Many women will be fascinated by these fake expressions. But they do not know that, when the real behavior of these people is completely contrary to moral standards, no matter how well they talk, how much money they have in their pockets, it is just a mask of deception! Buddha Dharma is to point out the truth about human life, and its most basic content is: Law of cause and effect! Buddha's teachings point out that the root of all suffering is due to human greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, and doubt, along with endless karma sins caused by body, speech, and mind. Without sowing good causes, how can there be good results? Having sown evil causes, it is difficult to avoid evil consequences. Therefore, it is necessary to quickly abandon evil, turn towards good, believe deeply in cause and effect, keep the five precepts, practice the ten good deeds, sow good causes to receive good results! Hopefully more people will not be deceived by propaganda against humanity in modern society,
Don't be superstitious anymore, wake up soon and clearly realize the truth of life. Even after hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, the karma created will not be lost. When causes and conditions converge, the retribution will still have to be borne!
Reminder: Buddhists take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha in order to learn Buddha's right knowledge and right view. They must practice according to the teachings, not go everywhere asking for protection or miraculous powers. Layman Vuong's experience tells everyone that: Learning Buddha must be practiced from the heart, eliminating greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, etc., these habits, correcting evil habits, and keeping strict precepts to truly enjoy the benefits.

tieu_de: chanting sutras, reciting mantras, NIFIM Buddha SPECIALIZED MIND
tom_tat: In the Forty-Twelve Chapter Sutra, Buddha said: "If you control your mind in one place, nothing will fail." Reciting mantras chanting sutras is precious in capturing the mind. Lately, due to being particularly busy with work and study, when doing evening classes, chanting sutras K...
noi_dung:
In the Forty-Twelve Chapter Sutra, Buddha said: "If you control your mind in one place, nothing will fail." Reciting mantras chanting sutras is precious in capturing the mind. Recently, due to being particularly busy with work and study, when doing the evening class, chanting the Vajra Sutras and the Shurangama Mantra, I often have many delusions and cannot concentrate. One day, I suddenly had a delusion: The Buddha Sutras say that when we chant the sutras, countless sentient beings will come to listen to the sutras and the dharma. Is this true? As soon as my thoughts started, in the high left corner, suddenly many heavenly soldiers, heavenly generals and gods appeared, they were standing and looking at me. I was startled and thought to myself: Oh my! The Buddha's words in the sutra are not wrong at all, we really are not allowed to doubt even the slightest bit. At this point, I got rid of all delusions, did not dare to have any distracting thoughts, and began chanting the sutras single-mindedly without distraction.
Some people come to the temple to make offerings the Three Jewels, to help print scriptures, and they must ask people to write their names, thinking that only then will they have merit. Asking for merit like that is stupid! Why write your name? If you write your name, your merit will no longer be great. If you don't write your name, you will have merit. Have you ever thought about it? When you write your name on the back of the sutra book or merit board, everyone who comes to listen to the sutra kneels here. After listening to the sutra, everyone comes to worship this sutra. Your name is written on the back of the prayer book, on the merit table, which means you are also receiving everyone's worship. What merits do you have? Are you worthy of receiving respect from others?
"The monk has no virtue, accepting worship is a lie." If you do not have great virtue, you cannot arbitrarily accept offerings from others. Venerable Master Hsuan Hua was 78 years old, in poor health, lying in bed. The attendant said: "Master, there is a guest from California who wants to come see you." Master said: "Oh, help me up, bring my shirt here." I said: "Master, you're not feeling well, you don't need to wear the robe." The Venerable replied: "No, they came to worship me. We are not qualified to accept worship from others. When we put on the robe, they worship, that is worshiping Buddha. The robe symbolizes Buddha." "If I don't explain clearly, I will be guilty."
You see, Venerable Master Hsuan Hua is so old that he has to wear a robe to dare to accept his worship.
other. What about us now? What I say, think for yourself. Even those leaving the home life, not everyone can arbitrarily accept offerings from others. They must wear a robe to receive offerings. I don't know what it is like in our country. But are you virtuous enough to accept the worship of others? There are many people who want to worship me, so I say: "If you continue to worship, I won't sit here anymore, I'll go." Therefore, I must place a Buddha statue in front of me. If there is no Buddha statue, I must place a prayer book. You are worshiping the Buddha statue, worshiping the scripture, not worshiping me. Since I do not have that virtue, I cannot accept your worship. Receiving other people's worship is the biggest dissipation of blessings!
Doing good deeds will definitely have good results. All the good things we have done and helped others will definitely bring blessings. The more you don't think about the blessings, the greater the blessings. If you do it for the sake of retribution, otherwise there will be no retribution. For example, today I did a good deed, helping a blind man cross the street. He still needed money, so I gave him ten coins. You do such a good job, everyone you meet says: “Hey Mr. Trieu, today I helped a blind man cross the street. And give him ten dong." You tell this person or that person, initially Buddha intended to give you 100% merit, but when you say it, there is only 10% merit left. Say it one more time, and you will no longer have merit. If you continue to talk, you will become a person with no merit, on the contrary, you will have negative merit, thus lacking virtue. Nowadays, there are many people who do not understand this.
Recently on TV there was an old man riding a tricycle to rent passengers, a very ordinary person, but when he passed away, many people across the country remembered him. Why is that? After retiring, he started riding a three-wheeled bicycle to carry passengers, and donated the money he earned to build schools in poor areas. He is over 80 years old and still rides his bike
three cakes, every morning after eating, his wife prepares him dumplings, he takes them with him to work. When he's hungry, he eats this cake, but can't bear to buy rice to eat outside. He donated the money he earned to build schools in difficult areas, and donated to teachers there to build bridges and roads. You see, he lived to be over 90 years old, and when he was hospitalized, his skin was still rosy and healthy. Therefore, if people do good deeds, heaven will protect them. This old man practiced very well and will be born in heaven, because in the Buddha Sutra it is said that cultivating the ten good karmas will in the future be born in heaven. Help others selflessly, and in the future you will be born in heaven. You will have whatever you want. If you want to eat delicious food, you will have it as soon as you think about it. What clothes do you want to wear? As soon as you think, clothes appear. Others say this is superstition, look at the high-tech products being exhibited at the current International Exhibition, just think, you want the computer to turn on, just think, "whoosh" sound, the computer turns on. For example, this door is closed, you just need to think to open it, as soon as you think, it will open. The safe, you think it opens right away. But this must be what you think, I think it can't be opened. Now that high technology has developed to this level, this is the "thought of success".
In today's world it is possible to do so, let alone in heaven. This old man, when he was still in the human world, used his hard-earned money to help others. After being born in heaven, if you want to eat, you will have it right away, if you want to wear it, you will have it right away. Heaven's clothes have no threads, and our clothes now have threads, because they are sewn by sewing machines. Clothes in the sky, just think about it, the high technology there is much more developed than our high technology. Everything there just needs to be thought to be there, the house in the sky is also just need to be thought to be there.
Why am I able to observe the precepts? It's because I understand the secret of cause and effect. Understanding this clearly, I don't dare to do anything selfish, only do things that benefit others.
other. I don't even have selfish thoughts anymore, I don't even dare to think about them. Even the thought "I am benefiting sentient beings", I don't have that thought. Whatever you do, everyone knows, there's nothing to worry about, just think that this is what you should do.
In the past I had too much debt, I am paying it off, I hope we all are too. Don't think that you are doing good deeds, you are doing good deeds. Don't seek fame, don't seek profit, you must think that no matter what good deed you do, you will not seek blessings, vowing to give all your blessings, dedicating merit to the unjust bondholders, dedicating merit to all sentient beings. Try doing that and see what good results you will receive.

tieu_de: NIFIM KY I MEET THE MASTER QU KHANH
tom_tat: After more than 7 hours of traveling, I finally met Mr. Qua Khanh. Right from the first floor, I heard the teacher's voice preaching the Dharma. Going upstairs, I saw a very large Buddha hall, filled with monks and lay people receiving ordination...
noi_dung:
After more than 7 hours of traveling, I finally met Mr. Qua Khanh. Right from the first floor, I heard the teacher's voice preaching the Dharma. Going upstairs, I saw a very large Buddha hall, filled with monks, lay people taking ordination and many admirers coming to listen to the sutras. I just heard the teacher say: "chanting sutras, reciting Buddha's name, if you don't cultivate your mind, you will still go to hell as usual."
Some people have pain in one area of their ankle, but seeing a doctor doesn't help. The teacher observed his diseased area, saw that the skin and internal tissues gradually became transparent, appearing before his eyes was a group of black spots. Looking more closely, it turned out to be a colony of ants. "Of course this is the spirit of ants." The teacher asked him if he had ever harmed ants. He's right, he has crushed many ants to death.
There was a girl with lumps on her arms like half a quail egg. The teacher gently asked her if she had ever stolen things from the temple. She was right, she took a lot. The teacher said: "You should sincerely repentance and never do it again, otherwise the consequences will be very serious."
When Master Qua Khanh thought about Venerable Master Hsuan Hua's past life, immediately before his eyes appeared the image of a very large, white-clothed person. Looking up, he saw that it was Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva of immeasurable compassion. From then on, we know that Venerable Master Hsuan Hua is the reincarnation of Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara.
It was his daughter, Qua Lam, who led him onto the path of studying Buddhism. Your daughter's wisdom is much greater than yours
many. One day, two neighbors couldn't find a mature Treasury bond and were so worried that they fell ill. Qua Lam pointed out where the bond was to his grandparents, and they quickly found it. At that time, he thought, girls can see even a hidden bond, so what else can't be seen? So the teacher said to his wife: “From now on, don't touch me, and I won't touch you anymore. Even though the girl is in the next room, she can see everything."
Cutting off lust and eliminating craving is the basis. The true joy after giving up desire cannot be expressed in words.
Because he had to take the bus home in the afternoon, Master Qua Khanh cleverly refused those who wanted to ask him more questions and returned with the Dharma Masters to their room to rest. Because he had been teaching the Dharma all morning and was very tired, I only asked him a few questions. He said that your destiny is decided by yourself. If you make an effort to do good and practice well, your life will be extended. Others cannot do it for you; Reciting and reciting the Ksitigarbha Sutra can be done at any time.
During the heat of the summer, he taught the Dharma in Jilin for a while, then for everyone's sake, he went to Shenyang with great difficulty, which was really arduous. Before coming, I bought him a set of clothes to wear at home. After buying them, I even washed them once, because unlike outer clothes, when I buy them, I should wash them before wearing them. Waiting for the teacher to finish eating, I gave it to him, but he refused. Before that, I had also heard that he preached the Dharma in Jilin until his voice was hoarse, so I bought Golden Lotus and Herbal Conch lozenges, but he also did not accept them. The teacher said his voice was fine. Amitabha Buddha.
The teacher didn't accept anything, for some reason I just wanted to cry, the tears just kept flowing. The teacher gently patted my shoulder and said: "Okay, okay, stop crying." At the urging of the Magicians, he went to rest in the rec room. I walked out alone, trying not to cry anymore. I don't know why I'm like that, the feeling is hard to describe.
Under the introduction of layperson Truong in Shenyang, I happened to meet the teacher's wife before the afternoon lecture. Even though she is 60 years old, she is still very beautiful and dignified, white-skinned, gentle and kind. I held the nun's hand, asked a few questions, and then went with her to the Buddhist temple. She said she stayed to do the laundry and take care of him. When the teacher preached the Dharma, the mother sat in the audience's row. The caring and clear eyes of the teacher when looking at him touched me very much. I sincerely hope that the teacher and the teacher will always be happy and healthy, and attain Bodhi together.
During the afternoon lecture, the teacher coughed a few times but couldn't stop. He spoke in a very hoarse voice. This made me worried. I quietly left the Kim Lien Hoa and the lozenges with the lay practitioner Ho Dharma, asking him to pass them on to him. Oh, the teacher travels everywhere for everyone's sake, regardless of hardships and teachings, helping many people enter the true path of learning Buddha. Bodhisattva's vow makes others admire him. After only listening to the sermon for half an hour, I regretfully left the Buddha hall. When I went downstairs, I could still hear the teacher's voice. Amitabha Buddha, my tears keep falling again. Looking out at the wheat field outside the car, I always remember what my teacher said to me: "Must observe the precepts, observe the precepts very well."

tieu_de: AFTER Wu Zetian's Passage, She Went Away
tom_tat:
After Wu Zetian passed away, where did she go: No matter how great the reward, creating evil karma is difficult to avoid falling
When we open the sutras, we will often see a verse to open the sutra. This verse was written when the 80 volumes of...
noi_dung:
After Wu Zetian passed away, where did she go: No matter how great the reward, creating evil karma is difficult to avoid falling
When we open the sutras, we will often see a verse to open the sutra. This verse was written when the 80 volumes of the Avatamsaka Sutra were completely translated into Chinese and presented to the emperor (at that time the emperor was Wu Zetian of the Wu Zhou dynasty). Vo Tac Thien wrote these four verses of "Sutra opening verse" so excellently that later many monks and monks also wanted to compose another verse but could not do so; Up to now, no one has been able to write a better verse to open the sutra.
Therefore, the opening verse of the sutra that we often read before each sutra book is the verse written when the Avatamsaka Sutra was completely translated. Wu Zetian, deeply feeling the magic and rarity of the meaning of the sutra, was very happy and inspired to write the opening verse of this sutra.
“Sutra opening verse
Supremely profound and wonderful dharma, encountered in thousands of thousands of lifetimes; The golden knowledge of the text is attained and maintained,
In Buddhism there is a story like this. Twenty-five hundred years ago, when Shakyamuni Buddha Buddha was still alive, one day, Shakyamuni Buddha led his disciples to beg for alms. A group of children are playing with sand on the road. Among them, there was a pretty little girl. From afar, she saw Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha leading his disciples. She half-jokingly and half-seriously used both hands to pick up a handful of sand from the ground, walked in front of the Buddha and placed it in his bowl. Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha compassionately accepted the little girl's handful of sand.
Great disciple Sariputta saw this and was dissatisfied, thinking that this girl was unreasonable, how could she use sand to jokingly make offerings with the Buddha. On the way, I couldn't help but ask: “Dear Tathagata, just now that girl put sand in your bowl, how could you let her play and be so naughty?”
Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha smiled: "You don't know, this girl hundreds of years later, when the destiny is ripe, will become king in the kingdom of Dong Chan Dan (China). If I don't accept her sand now, later when she becomes king she will find every way to sabotage Buddha Dharma. I accept this sand so that she can sow good fortune, and later when she becomes king, she will protect and propagate Buddha Dharma."
That girl later became Wu Zetian in Chinese history. Right from birth, she had the appearance of a king. Before becoming queen, Vo Ze Thien worked as a nun for four or five years. She not only believes in Buddha's teachings but is also proficient in Buddha's teachings.
She composed a four-line verse praising Buddha's teachings: Regarding the origin of this verse, there is a legend that when Wu Zetian became emperor, because she was a very devout Buddhist and loved the Avatamsaka Sutra. She always felt
The Jin Dynasty's translation of the Avatamsaka Sutra was lacking in many parts and was incomplete, so she felt very regretful. Therefore, a special envoy was sent to India to request this sutra to see if there was a complete version. At that time, the Tripitaka Dharma Master of Vu Dien country had this sutra, and she immediately invited this Dharma Master to return to China with him. That Dharma Master is Thuc Xoa Nanda. After inviting Thuc Xoa Nanda back, she invited him to preside over the translation of the Avatamsaka Sutra.
Thuc Xoa Nan Da Dharma Master in the Western Region is a Dharma Master with great virtue. The great men in China, including the emperors, all admired him. The emperor himself personally invited Dharma Master Thuc Xoa Nanda to China.
When Dharma Master Thuc Xoa Nanda came, he brought with him the Avatamsaka Sutra, which, although not complete, had nine thousand more chants than the Jin translation, so there were a total of forty-five thousand chants, and the great meaning of the sutra could be clearly seen. The translation work was very large-scale, and Wu Zetian himself was often involved.
After completing the translation, when Wu Zetian read the Avatamsaka Sutra for the first time, she felt the magic and rarity of Buddha's teachings and was very happy. Therefore, she was moved to write the opening verse for this great sutra. This is the opening verse of the sutra that we often recite today.
Wu Zetian, we all know she is the only legitimate female emperor in Chinese history. The period of Wu Zetian's reign was called "The righteous rise of Khai Nguyen, the reign of Trinh Quan", with the role of inheritance and development, laying the foundation for the "prosperity of Khai Nguyen" in the Middle Tang period.
Furthermore, Wu Zetian greatly respected Buddhism and played an important role in promoting and developing Buddhism.
Perhaps many people want to know where Vo Ze Thien, who was so powerful, was reincarnated after her death?
Master Lien Tri once wrote in his essay Truc Song: "Up to now, among the cats and mice, there are still two people, Vo Ze Thien and Tieu Thuc Phi, reincarnated. Even though they have taken revenge hundreds of thousands of times, they still have not stopped. In the past, when we held the Water and Green Tram Ceremony, out of pity, we delivered it to them. I'm just afraid that their resentment is too deep, and my deliverance effect is not great enough, and cannot be resolved immediately..."
Why is that? Emperor Cao Tong Ly Tri had a beloved concubine named Tieu Thuc Phi. Empress Vuong Thi, out of favor, wanted to defeat Tieu Thuc Phi, so she voluntarily offered to bring Vo Tac Thien into the harem.
Who would have thought that after Vo Ze Thien entered the palace, she quickly defeated Tieu Thuc Phi and Queen Vuong Thi. Not long after, Wu Zetian was made empress, and empress Wang Thi and Tieu Thuc Phi were both deposed as commoners.
After being detained, Queen Vuong Thi and Tieu Thuc Phi were locked in a tight room, with only a small hole for food. Duong Cao Tong secretly visited them. The two cried and told Duong Cao Tong: "I hope that your Majesty will think of the old friendship and let us see the sunlight again. We hope to change the name of the prison to 'Returning the Mind Institute', that is a blessing of rebirth!". Duong Cao Tong immediately agreed.
However, Vo Ze Thien found out and immediately ordered his men to beat Queen Vuong Thi and Tieu Thuc Phi 100 times each, then cut off all their arms and legs and throw them into a jar of wine, saying: "Soak in the bones of these two old women!"
Not long after, both people died tragically. Before he died, Tieu Thuc Phi swore an oath and scolded Vo Ze Thien: "May A Vo (Wu Tac Thien) turn into a mouse, I will become a cat. I will bite you to death forever and ever as revenge!"
This story is known to many people. Even though the blessings are as great as Wu Zetian, after creating evil karma, it is still difficult to avoid falling.
Tieu Thuc Phi had made such a vow, with such strong thoughts at the time of death, perhaps it was really difficult to escape the cycle of karma...
For thousands of years, people have only seen this part of history as a story. How many people would have thought that the injustice between themselves and others would be so difficult to resolve and entangle forever?
One thought of anger arises, thousands of barriers open. Once you have entered the path of practice, you must carefully protect your thoughts!

tieu_de: Venerable Hsuan Hua's COMMENTS ON CULTURED QU KHANH
tom_tat:
This is a public lecture by Venerable Master Hsuan Hua in a Dharma conference of thousands of people. The disciple edited and re-compiled based on the Venerable's recording.
When coming to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, everyone needs to know...
noi_dung:
This is a public lecture by Venerable Master Hsuan Hua in a Dharma conference of thousands of people. The disciple edited and re-compiled based on the Venerable's recording.
When people come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, they need to know why they came here. The world is so vast, why do so many people gather in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas? That's because each person's good roots are ripe and it's time to bloom and bear fruit. We meet here to learn together, exchange and sharpen each other. On the Bodhi path, there is only progress, no retreat. Even if you suffer a little, your future will be forever free from suffering. Therefore, I always remind people with two very simple sentences:
"To endure suffering is to end suffering, to enjoy happiness is to eliminate happiness."
If you have suffering and don't endure it, suffering will forever exist. If you have good fortune and don't spend it all, that good fortune will remain forever. That's why I said: "To endure suffering is to end suffering, to enjoy happiness is to eliminate happiness." I will repeat it again, lest you may forget these simple words. So, without hesitation I say it again: "To endure suffering is to end suffering, to enjoy happiness is to eliminate happiness." If you remember these two sentences carefully, then you can endure any suffering and you will not want to enjoy the blessings right away. You will want to preserve the blessing, not spend it all. This is something that practitioners should know.
Today, at noon, I still have many things I want to say to everyone but haven't finished them yet.
I have mentioned the layman Vimalakirti, but even Arhat did not dare to come and ask about his illness, because he had previously scolded him. There are many Bodhisattvas who do not dare to come. Finally, Bodhisattva Manjushri came and discussed with the lay practitioner Vimalakirti about the secret of practice. The two had a profound conversation. If you have not read the Vimalakirti Sutra, I recommend studying this passage. Those who have already read it should study more deeply to better understand this sutra.
Because here, in Tianjin, I invited this layman Duong, that is Duong Tac Tuong (or layman Qua Khanh). He can wholeheartedly study "Teaching Luc" and my other simple explanations. Although he did not necessarily read everything, in the process of educating his group of people (ie the group of Buddhist believers in Tianjin), more than a hundred people were influenced by him to come to Buddhism. Believing in Buddha is also normal, and one hundred people is not a large number, everywhere a few hundred people who believe in Buddha can gather. But although it is said that mainland China has religious freedom, in fact no religion dares to openly preach. Yet, the group of more than a hundred people of lay practitioner Duong, it can be said that they regularly gather at private homes, go to lay practitioner Duong's house to study Buddha dharma.
During this time, it was unexpected that there were more than twenty people who achieved heavenly eye penetration, heavenly ear penetration, other-mind penetration, fate-fulfilling power, and supernatural power. They all achieved these types of "passes". They are not people leaving the home life, but lay people, with sincerity learning Buddha Dharma, and achieving this practice.
As for me, in America for more than thirty years, I have achieved nothing. Although there are some people who believe in Buddha, there are not many people who truly believe in Buddha, most of them just stop at the superficial level. They say leaving the home life but they don't have the appearance of someone leaving the home life, their posture is not good, their attitude is also not good. All are in the "substandard" category.
I thought, why do I have disciples like this? Well, it turns out it's because I - the teacher - don't know how to educate people. That's why we can't teach talented people. Therefore, I feel extremely ashamed every day, feeling incapable of educating others. But we cannot give up, we must continue to educate, continue, continue without stopping. Whether or not I know how to educate, I must fulfill my responsibility with sincerity. Therefore, for many years now, I have only been waiting for young, talented Buddhists to come here to promote Buddha Dharma.
Having waited for so many years, now the group of people in Tianjin probably also have fate with me. For now, I want to invite them here. But "good things often encounter difficulties", when they applied for a visa, the Embassy refused to issue a visa. Even so, I was not discouraged, continued to make efforts and think differently. I intend to invite these seven people here to prepare for a religious conference. I want to invite all religions in the world, regardless of sect, religious order or sect, to come here and participate. I plan to take care of all travel and accommodation expenses for those coming from far away. No matter how much money it costs, I will be responsible. In addition, I also plan to invite famous professors and scholars from universities to participate, to directly discuss the truth of Buddhism and the direction of salvation. We need to discuss ways to save the world, save the country, save the people, help sentient beings escape the ocean of suffering to reach a realm of peace and joy.
Ultimate Bliss. This idea is very important, so everyone here must do part of the work of protecting the ashram. No one should back down, nor should they be lazy or try to avoid responsibility. Everyone must make diligent efforts and achieve achievements in order to propagate Buddha Dharma. If you don't have achievements, if you don't have genuine practice, then you cannot propagate Buddha Dharma.
Today I plan to rest a bit, because yesterday I preached three times, and the day before yesterday I preached three times. Since the beginning until now, I have preached seven or eight times. Layman Duong also felt tired, and I also felt very tired. So tonight I plan to rest. Unexpectedly, someone wouldn't let us rest. He said he wanted to talk to everyone tonight, so fine, we'll rest a little less and do a little more work. You should listen carefully, don't be careless and fall asleep. If you doze off, our hard work will be wasted. We speak to benefit you, otherwise there would be no reason to speak. If you don't pay attention, these words will be like wind blowing in your ears and won't be of any help. I won't say much today. After the translator finishes translating, I will invite layman Duong to endure a little more hardship.
(Female voice continues...)
Just now I mentioned that each person has "five types of eyes". Some people will wonder: "Oh, why don't I have one?". Actually, it's not that you don't have it, it's that you haven't protected and trained it properly. Everyone has five types of eyes. But we don't know how to practice, and no one guides us to realize it. Therefore, in the eyes of the Bodhisattva and Arhat, we are all the same as the blind, no different from the visually impaired. Why
So? Because we have not opened the heavenly eye, the physical eye, the dharma eye, the wisdom eye, and the Buddha eye. If you have not opened it, you have no right to doubt those who have opened it.
As I said, the group of people in Tianjin had more than twenty people who opened the five types of eyes within four to five years. Not thanks to anything else, but thanks to them being sincere, wholeheartedly respecting the Buddha, and always remembering the Buddha, never forgetting to practice for a moment. Buddha, with his compassion and joy, helped them achieve this feat. You can also try it.
If you want to open the five types of eyes, lay people Yang can help you. What kind of person wouldn't be able to open his eyes? Those are people who are not sincere and do not believe. As the saying goes: "Those who have a little doubt will not be able to achieve results." Therefore, I hope everyone will have the will to serve Buddhism, work for Buddhism, educate sentient beings, and help Buddhism take root in the West, sprout, sprout leaves, and bear fruit. Those who study Buddhism in the West must take on this responsibility.
Those of you who have sincerity will be able to open it. Don't doubt that: “Oh, is this a dream? Or am I delusional? Are these realms real or not?". That's not true. If you are sincere, with just one sincere thought, you can overcome three great Asanga kalpas in an instant and achieve what you desire.
I'm just saying this. It's up to you to listen or not, just pretend I didn't say anything. Believe it or not, it's okay, I'm not forcing you.
(Female voice translates...)
Layperson Qua Khanh: Today I have the opportunity to sit here, in the Great Hall of the Ten Thousand Buddhas,
is what I always wished for. A few years ago, I watched a videotape, which was the tape recording the scene of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. That was the time the Chinese Buddhist delegation came to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to worship and participate in the Great Dharma Conference of Water and Green Emptiness. A few years ago, I was very fortunate to have that tape and when I saw the solemn image of the Dai Hung Bao Palace, I thought that if in the future I had the opportunity to come here and pay homage to the Buddha, it would be a great honor. But that's just an illusion, I absolutely don't believe it can become reality. I didn't expect that I would actually be sitting here today.

tieu_de: DISCUSSING enlightenment
tom_tat:
I never thought that the sentence: "A person who is truly enlightened will not say he has enlightenment" - a saying full of wisdom like that, but people consider it a heresy.
I'm just a small student at Buddha's door, with no qualifications...
noi_dung:
I never thought that the sentence: "A person who is truly enlightened will not say he has enlightenment" - a saying full of wisdom like that, but people consider it a heresy.
I'm just a small student at Buddha's door, and I'm not qualified to discuss profound issues like enlightenment, but now I can't help but reluctantly say a few words.
First of all, let's talk about how I understand enlightenment. "Enlightenment" means beginning, "enlightenment" is thinking and understanding deeper than just "thinking". This is a special term of Buddhism, referring to the breakthrough enhancement of the realm of thought of Buddhist practitioners when they understand a certain truth. From not understanding to understanding, from confusion to starting enlightenment, from not believing in Buddha to believing in Buddha, then from believing in Buddha to learning Buddha, that is the enlightenment process that takes place little by little. Therefore, the word "enlightenment" includes the process of a person beginning to realize the path, not just used for those who have cultivated to Arhat or Bodhisattva, and to become Buddha is to reach complete enlightenment.
If Bodhisattva or Arhat incarnates into the world, when the cause and effect to save people is ripe, under the blessing of Buddha's power, they may be enlightened because of a sutra, an illness, or meeting an enlightened person, or a dream. At that time, wisdom abilities will appear and begin to propagate Dharma to save people. Buddha dharma naturally flows from their own nature, so people with such great capacity do not need to penetrate the scriptures to understand the principles. This enlightenment
called "sudden enlightenment", from ordinary people suddenly becoming saints. There were people at that time who knew clearly who they were when they returned to the human world, but would never reveal the truth, because if they revealed their identity, they would be worshiped by everyone, making offerings every day, and could not be an example for sentient beings on the path of studying Buddha Dharma for enlightenment. Like Shakyamuni Buddha, he was originally a Buddha, but he appeared as a mortal, became a prince, got married and had children, went out to the four doors and encountered the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death at all doors. From there, enlightenment began. In the end, he gave up his glory, wealth and position as future king, left his beloved wife and precious child, and went to the mountains to practice Buddhism. The six years of asceticism that he practiced was a pagan dharma that sought outside the mind, even eating only one sesame seed or barley grain a day, almost starving to death, but in the end he did not achieve it. Finally, he let go of all his fate and under the Bodhi tree suddenly became Buddha (sudden enlightenment also comes from gradual enlightenment). The Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha had practiced Buddhahood countless previous lives, so why did he have to go through such an arduous practice process to achieve it? It is to set an example for us in the future to see that to become a Buddha we must let go of delusions and attachments. Only a pure mind can attain it. Today, Bodhisattva and Arhat were sent by the Buddha to the human world during the end of the world to help enlighten sentient beings.
It is absolutely unnecessary to declare to everyone that: "I have enlightenment", unless the sentient beings' basic abilities at that time require a teacher to clearly identify their identity and background to easily be saved, as in the case of Tibetan Tantric disciples, before taking refuge in the Buddha, taking refuge in the Dharma, taking refuge in the Sangha, then there is also the additional part of "taking refuge in the guru". Ordinary people's practice and enlightenment cannot be compared with the enlightenment of the returning Bodhisattva and Arhat.
Let's take the example of a child with poor moral qualities. Through the education of his teachers, one day he finally understands human morality and is determined to change and become a new person. This can be considered an "enlightenment". After that, this child continued to learn and improve, becoming an excellent student. Then he became a doctor, a big businessman, and even a pillar of the nation. Each of these advancements is a process of raising the realm of thought, and I compare each time to an "enlightenment". In worldly dharma, every advancement and progress like that, we ourselves know and others also know, because it is something everyone can see clearly. But in the dharma of the world, we ourselves do not know. Every time you understand a principle, apart from the feeling of joy at that moment, you certainly cannot know that: "A! I have already attained enlightenment, I have attained a certain state."
If you say you have attained Arhat, or have attained Bodhisattva, you are lying to deceive people, because Arhat and Bodhisattva are both free of ego. If you say "I have enlightenment", there is still "I", meaning you have not enlightenment. If you say "I have attained the first fruit, the second fruit, the third fruit, the fourth fruit or the Bodhisattva fruition", then there is also "I", which is absolutely not the realm of Arhat and Bodhisattva. Yet if you tell people that you have attained enlightenment, have cultivated into Arhat or Bodhisattva, aren't you lying to people? Your purpose is to trick other people's respect and make offerings. If that isn't evil, then what is?
A cultivator, if he has not achieved complete enlightenment and attained Buddhahood, will forever see his shortcomings. I will use magical powers as an example: You can cultivate the heavenly eye power, but if you don't have the heavenly ear power, you must
Cultivated the heavenly ear, but still did not have enough life; until you practice the five penetrations, but still lack complete penetration. Before becoming a Buddha, learning is endless, so a person who is truly enlightened and attains enlightenment will absolutely not brag about his supernatural powers in front of the crowd, unless he is forced to display them in order to save sentient beings. But even if they appear, they will not say they are "enlightened", because whether or not a cultivator has enlightenment is first judged based on that person's virtue. If you have a bit of fame or extraordinary ability and take advantage of it for profit or to intimidate others, or claim to be the leader of the world, greedy for fame and fortune and deceive others, then it is definitely an evil spirit coming to the world.
Second, listen to see if their teachings are in accordance with Buddha's teachings. If not, it is heresy. Saying: "To deviate from the scriptures by even one word is a heresy; to interpret it according to the text is unjust to all three generations of Buddhas."
Third, it needs to be certified by current enlightened monks, through the eyes of their wisdom. If you are a saint who has attained enlightenment, you will know just by meeting him, or by just hearing him talk, or by just hearing his name, you will know; Even pagan scholars recognized it immediately.
Therefore, the fact that Hue Kha "enlightened as soon as he heard the words" was not only the confirmation of Patriarch Bodhidharma at that time, but also the recognition of the four assemblies' disciples with Hue Kha. This is not because Hue Kha himself said: "I have enlightenment". Similarly, the enlightenment of old Venerable Hu Van when "the cup of tea fell to the ground" was also the recognition of the disciples of the four groups at that time, and of course also the recognition of enlightened monks and wise men of the time, posterity, as well as today. For example, the Sixth Patriarch Hui Neng was not
was certified by Fifth Patriarch Hoang Nhan when he recited the verse "Bodhi has no tree, no mirror, no platform, no object, no place is covered with dust"? And "listening to a sutra, the mind is immediately enlightened" is only the beginning of Huineng's enlightenment. Think about it, after Hui Neng heard the phrase "If you don't have a place to live, you will be born with a strange mind" and attained enlightenment, why did you still need the certification of the Five Patriarchs? If you immediately say: "I have enlightenment, I can become a Patriarch", I think those who heard at that time would definitely think that this person was possessed by evil spirits or crazy.
There is another story in Buddhism, related to the enlightenment poem by layperson Su Dongpo: "Paying homage to the enlightenment, his halo shines across the sky, the eight winds blow without moving, he sits firmly on the golden lotus."
Layperson To Dongpo considered himself enlightened, claiming that the eight winds of benefit - failure, destruction - hesitation, confession - opportunity, suffering - pleasure could not move his mind, as if he had sat or was about to sit on the lotus and become Bodhisattva, Buddha. However, he could not stand the challenge of the four words "farting, farting" (farting, farting) from the Venerable Buddha An, causing his statement to be rejected.
Therefore, enlightenment or not enlightenment, achievement or lack of Arhat, Bodhisattva, not only needs the confirmation of wise people but also must be verified through practice. My statements cannot be considered evidence. Even the "authentication" of "great monks" is not necessarily correct. Because in the era of "the enemy wears Tathagata's clothes to trade Dharma", who will verify whether the great virtues are truly great virtues, whether the wisdom of the great monks is truly noble? Therefore, only practice is the standard for testing enlightenment and achieving results.
The realm of Arhat and Maha Bodhisattva has been recorded in Buddhist scriptures. The disciples of the four groups have the ability to distinguish, not to mention enlightenment and attainment are to teach sentient beings to escape from the ocean of suffering. When you have wisdom to propagate the Dharma to benefit yourself, that is enough, there is no need to advertise yourself saying: "I have enlightenment"?
Let us remember the Buddha's teachings in the Diamond Sutra: "Hey Tu Bodhi, what do you think? Do you think that you have achieved Sotapanna status? Tu Bodhi replied: No, venerable sir. Why is that? Because Sotapanna is called 'stream-entering' without any place to enter, not entering form, sound, smell, taste, touch, dharma, so it is called Sotapanna". And "Tu Da Ham is called a return, but there really is no return, so it is called Tu Da Ham". "A Na Ham is called no return, but there really is no such thing as no return, so it is called A Na Ham." "There really is no dharma called Arhat. World-Honored One, if Arhat thinks that he has attained Arhat, then there is attachment to self, attachment to others, attachment to sentient beings, attachment to recipients. World-Honored One, Buddha said that I have achieved unobstructed Samadhi, am the highest among human beings, and am the most secluded Arhat. World-Honored One, I do not think that I am an Arhat renounced from desire. World-Honored One, if I had thought that I had attained the path of Arhat, then the World-Honored One would not have said that Tu Bodhi is one who loves the practice of Arhat, because Tu Bodhi really has no place to practice but is called Tu Bodhi who loves the practice of Arhat." "If Bodhisattva still accepts the appearance of self, the appearance of people, the appearance of living beings, and the appearance of receiving beings, then it is not Bodhisattva."
The Buddha's teachings above are enough to show that a true practitioner absolutely no longer clings to ego. If there is still a form of ego, then it is only an ordinary person, and certainly not an enlightened person. Enlightenment or not enlightenment, attainment or not attainment, or what result has been attained, are just things
Just a noun, no entity. If there is an "I", then there will be treatment of others, a distinction between self and others. When there is the appearance of sentient beings, there is also the appearance of living beings. When these "four generals" still exist, they are not enlightened people! A person who is truly enlightened will never claim to be enlightened. "There is a natural scent of musk, there is no need for strong winds to blow it away!". Therefore, Venerable Hu Van certainly will not "declare to others that he has enlightenment". Otherwise, the old Venerable would not have said such deeply touching words as: "I'm still very far from practicing well. Everything I say is the words of the ancients. I tricked Buddha into eating for more than a hundred years" when the four groups invited him to teach.
Furthermore, "enlightenment" is not simply having the heavenly eye, the heavenly ear or certain "transmissions", because pagan evil spirits also have these "perceptions" and those "perceptions". A true practitioner, truly enlightened, must definitely have true wisdom to "contemplate often, not to make mistakes". While pagan evil spirits, although they have heavenly eyes, do not have wisdom, they are only greedy for fame and fortune, lie that they have enlightenment, and speak false statements, which is no different from "carving human feces into the shape of a sandalwood, hoping for a fragrant scent, that is impossible".
Venerable Master Hsuan Hua was the first person to spread Buddha dharma to the West. His teachings are very simple and easy to understand, have brought countless sentient beings to the correct path of learning Buddha, and are welcomed by the majority of Buddhists around the world. They respected him as a Saint. Many disciples had seen him in the moment of manifesting the form of Amitabha Buddha. There are even wise people who, when thinking about who Venerable Master Hsuan Hua is, immediately see the image of Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara appear in their minds or before their eyes. Because Buddha and Bodhisattva are inherently one, moreover
They often appear in all kinds of bodies to save sentient beings, so there is no need to be attached to this. Upon hearing about that, the Venerable said: "I'm not a saint at all. I am just a small ant, may all sentient beings pass through my body and enter the realm of Ultimate Bliss."
Thêm vào đó, Hòa thượng Tuyên Hóa được Hòa thượng Hư Vân, một đại tôn giả trong Thiền tông, xác nhận là người thừa kế pháp của tông phái Quy Ngưỡng đời thứ chín. If it is said that Venerable Master Hsuan Hua's teachings "distorted Buddha Dharma, defamed, denied and even destroyed Zen school and meditation masters", wouldn't it be saying that Venerable Hu Van did not have the eye of wisdom and was not an enlightened person? Saying so also means denying all predecessors, including Patriarch Bodhidharma. So let me ask, who is "the one who distorted Buddha Dharma, defamed, denied and destroyed Zen school and meditation masters" for thousands of generations?
Not to mention a lay person, but even a person leaving the home life, if he publicly posts an article that distorts and defames a noble monk who preached sutras and dharma all his life and saved countless sentient beings, he has committed the crime of disrupting monk harmony, an unimaginably great crime.
Did you know, after Venerable Master Hsuan Hua passed away, before he was cremated, his normal body suddenly turned purple-brown, making his disciples extremely surprised, so they quickly called to ask about Venerable Dieu Phap who was in China at that time. Venerable Dieu Phap immediately replied: "In front of my eyes appeared four golden words 'Tu demon golden body' (Golden body polished from purple jade)". This made the Venerable's disciples turn from confusion to joy, receiving great encouragement and increasing their confidence. Venerable Master Hsuan Hua also did
A verse appeared in the air for Venerable Dieu Phap to see while he was lying in bed:
"The old monk is so leisurely that he has nothing to do. He's caught playing hide-and-seek and lying here sick. His chest is full of boundless ambition. His frown concentrates the light.
Uncomfortably, he leans back and lifts his head. The benefits of saving sentient beings will never be forgotten. Forever looking for someone in the crowd. I don't know how to face each other and ponder forever.
If you see, there is no seeing, there is no non-emptiness, Ask about the illness to see the source, the source is not the source, Dependent on the corresponding conditions, there is no birth and death,
"The golden body is polished from purple jade" and this verse is completely true, if I lie, I will fall into hell. I write this to the author of the erroneous essay that said that Venerable Master Hsuan Hua is an evil spirit. They should sincerely repentance and take effective measures to remove the influence. Otherwise, evil views, false rumors, abusive attacks, and spreading evil theories will bring retribution. Furthermore, as long as this erroneous article exists in the world, it will mislead others.

tieu_de: MY PROBLEM IS CONSTRUCTION DISEASE

noi_dung:

innate stupidity". From childhood to adulthood, every time I saw my daughter, I blushed, my language was clumsy, and I was not good at expressing myself. wisdom is inconceivable, skill in means is inconceivable. If you don't mind, what are you waiting for!!!
